===Arizona Cardinals===
====2005====
The [[Arizona Cardinals]] selected Rolle in the first round (eighth overall) of the [[2005 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2005 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2005/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-07 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Rolle was the second cornerback drafted in 2005, behind [[Adam Jones (American football)|Adam "Pacman" Jones]].

On August 6, 2005, the Arizona Cardinals signed Rolle to a six-year, $43 million contract that includes $7.75 million guaranteed.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Antrel Rolle contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/chicago-bears/antrel-rolle-991/ |access-date=June 6, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Over the cap: Antrel Rolle contract |url=https://overthecap.com/player/antrel-rolle/849 |access-date=June 6, 2018 |website=Overthecap.com}}</ref>

Head coach [[Dennis Green]] named Rolle a starting cornerback to begin the regular season, alongside [[David Macklin]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Pro-Football-Reference: Arizona Cardinals Roster (2005) |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/crd/2005_roster.htm |access-date=June 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He made his professional regular season debut and first career start in the [[2005 Arizona Cardinals|Arizona Cardinals']] season-opener at the [[2005 New York Giants|New York Giants]] and recorded one tackle in their 42–19 loss. On September 25, 2005, Rolle collected a season-high 11 combined tackles (ten solo) during a 37–12 loss at the [[2005 Seattle Seahawks|Seattle Seahawks]] in Week 3. During the game, Rolle sustained an injury that was believed to be [[cartilage]] damage in his left [[knee]] and was scheduled to undergo surgery and miss 3–4 weeks. On October 3, 2005, Dr. John Uribe performed [[arthroscopic]] surgery on Rolle's knee to ostensibly repair the [[meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]] cartilage, but discovered ligament damage that was expected to sideline him for the rest of his rookie season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cards rookie Rolle out for season with knee injury |url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/columns/story?columnist=pasquarelli_len&id=2180116 |access-date=June 6, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |author=Pasquerelli, Len |date=October 3, 2005}}</ref> Rolle quickly recovered and returned after missing nine games (Weeks 4–13).<ref>{{cite web |title=Roethlisberger has thumb injury |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2005-dec-02-sp-nflrep2-story.html |access-date=June 6, 2018 |website= [[Los Angeles Times]] |date=December 2, 2005}}</ref> On December 11, 2005, Rolle recorded a solo tackle, a pass deflection, and made his first career interception in the Cardinals' 17–13 loss to the [[2005 Washington Redskins|Washington Redskins]]. His interception came off a deflection by tight end [[Chris Cooley (American football)|Chris Cooley]] who was unable to secure a pass thrown by quarterback [[Mark Brunell]] in the second quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=In Defense of the Offense |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2005/12/14/AR2005121402270.html |access-date=June 6, 2018 |website=washingtonpost.com |author=Bryant, Howard |date=December 15, 2005}}</ref> The following week, he collected nine solo tackles and broke up a pass during a 30–19 loss to the [[2005 Houston Texans|Houston Texans]] in Week 15. He aggravated his knee injury during the game and sidelined him for the last two games of the regular season (Weeks 16–17).<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Injury Report |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2005/12/29/nfl-injury-report-126/ |website=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |date=December 29, 2005 |access-date=June 7, 2018 |archive-date=June 12, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612140131/http://articles.baltimoresun.com/2005-12-29/sports/0512290213_1_knee-ankle-courtney-brown |url-status=live }}</ref> Rolle completed his rookie season in [[2005 NFL season|2005]] with 28 combined tackles (26 solo), a pass deflection, and an interception in five games and four starts.<ref name="career">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antrel Rolle (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antrelrolle/2506347/careerstats |access-date=June 6, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2006====
[[File:Rocknrolle.jpg|thumb|upright=1.1|Rolle with the [[Arizona Cardinals]], 2005]]
Defensive coordinator [[Clancy Pendergast]] retained Rolle and David Macklin as the starting cornerbacks to start the 2006 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Football Database: Arizona Cardinals Roster (2006) |url=https://www.footballdb.com/teams/nfl/arizona-cardinals/roster/2006?sort=pos |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=footballdb.com}}</ref> In Week 5, he collected eight solo tackles and a season-high two pass deflections in the Cardinals' 23–20 loss to the [[2006 Kansas City Chiefs|Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref name="stats6"/> On December 17, 2006, Rolle recorded a season-high 11 combined tackles (nine solo) and broke up a pass during a 37–20 loss to the [[2006 Denver Broncos|Denver Broncos]] in Week 15.<ref name="stats6">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antrel Rolle (2006) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antrelrolle/2506347/gamelogs?season=2006 |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the season with 84 combined tackles (77 solo), ten passes defensed, two forced fumbles, and an interception in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref name="career"/> Rolle had issues in pass coverage and was called for seven pass interference penalties in 2006, tying [[2006 Baltimore Ravens|Baltimore Ravens']] cornerback [[Chris McAlister]] for the most in the league.<ref>{{cite web |title=Antrel Rolle Loses Starting Job |url=https://www.footballoutsiders.com/extra-points/2007/antrel-rolle-loses-starting-job |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=footballoutsiders.com |date=August 21, 2007}}</ref>

====2007====
On January 1, 2007, the Arizona Cardinals fired head coach Dennis Green after they completed the 2006 season with a 5–11 record.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cardinals fire coach Green after three years |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/01/01/AR2007010100316_pf.html |access-date=June 3, 2018 |website=washingtonpost.com |date=January 1, 2007}}</ref> Rolle entered training camp slated as a starting cornerback, but saw competition for his role from [[Eric Green (cornerback)|Eric Green]] and [[Roderick Hood]]. On August 18, 2008, Rolle had a disappointing performance and gave up a 39-yard touchdown reception to wide receiver [[Andre Johnson]] during a 33–20 loss to the [[2007 Houston Texans|Houston Texans]] in their second preseason game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Texans set preseason scoring mark against Cardinals |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/texans/Texans-set-preseason-scoring-mark-against-Cards-1807689.php |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=Chron.com |agency=Associated Press |date=August 18, 2007 }}{{Dead link|date=June 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Two days later, head coach [[Ken Whisenhunt]] announced that [[Roderick Hood]] would be replacing Rolle as the starting left cornerback after performing well during the preseason.<ref>{{Citation |last=Tulumello |first=Mike |date= August 20, 2007 |title= Cardinals notebook: Cornerback Rolle loses starting spot |newspaper= East Valley Tribune |url= http://www.eastvalleytribune.com/story/95501 |url-status=dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080107001824/http://www.eastvalleytribune.com/story/95501 |archive-date= January 7, 2008 }}</ref> Head coach Ken Whisenhunt officially announced Rolle as the third cornerback on the depth chart, behind Eric Green and Roderick Hood, to start the regular season. Rolle was also named the first-team nickelback.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Arizona Cardinals Depth Chart: 09/02/2007 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/17/ARZ |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

In Week 9, he collected a season-high ten combined tackles (seven solo) in the Cardinals' 17–10 loss at the [[2007 Tampa Bay Buccaneers|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. On November 18, 2007, Rolle recorded four combined tackles, three pass deflections, three interceptions, and returned two for touchdowns during a 35–27 win at the [[2007 Cincinnati Bengals|Cincinnati Bengals]]. He made all three interceptions off passes by quarterback [[Carson Palmer]] and returned one for a 54-yard touchdown and another for a 55-yard touchdown.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news/detail.php?PRKey=2085|title=The Official Site of the Arizona Cardinals|access-date=November 21, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090214044913/http://www.azcardinals.com/news/detail.php?PRKey=2085|archive-date=February 14, 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/boxscore?gid=20071118004 NFL - Arizona Cardinals/Cincinnati Bengals Box Score Sunday November 18, 2007 - Yahoo! Sports<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> His performance earned him NFC Defensive Player of the Week honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.azcentral.com/sports/cardinals/articles/1120rolle.html|title=Rolle gets defense award}}</ref> Rolle was promoted to starting cornerback prior to Week 13 and remained in the role after Eric Green was sidelined with an ankle injury for the last five games (Weeks 13–17).<ref>{{cite web |title=Arizona's guaranteed a non-winning season for 22nd time 23 years |url=https://www.douglasdispatch.com/sports/arizona-s-guaranteed-a-non-winning-season-for-nd-time/article_823eeadc-e29e-5a2d-9337-03e1a2b26a47.html |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=douglasdispatch.com |date=December 20, 2007 }}{{Dead link|date=June 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> On December 30, 2007, Rolle recorded two solo tackles, three pass deflections, two interceptions, and a touchdown during a 48–19 victory against the [[2007 St. Louis Rams|St. Louis Rams]]. He had a [[pick 6 (American football)|pick six]] after intercepting a pass by [[Marc Bulger]] and returned in it for a 47-yard touchdown in the third quarter. He finished with 62 combined tackles (52 solo), ten passes defensed, five interceptions, and three touchdowns in 16 games and eight starts.<ref name="career"/> Throughout the 2007 season, Rolle was mainly used as a nickelback before moving to outside cornerback for the last five games.

====2008====
On February 27, 2008, it was reported that the Arizona Cardinals would be moving Rolle to free safety for the [[2008 NFL season]] after he impressed as the nickelback in 2007.<ref>{{cite web |title=Offseason News |url=http://arizonacardinals.contentquake.com/page/16/ |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=ArizonaCardinals.com |date=February 27, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612140523/http://arizonacardinals.contentquake.com/page/16/ |archive-date=June 12, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> As the nickelback, he was tasked with covering the deep middle of the field multiple times as a sub-safety. He intercepted four passes from the nickel position in 2007. Rolle entered training camp slated as the ''de facto'' starting free safety after the Cardinals opted to release [[Terrence Holt]] during the offseason.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Scouts' Buzz |url=https://www.si.com/more-sports/2008/04/04/buzz |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=si.com |author=Bucky Brooks |date=April 4, 2008|author-link=Bucky Brooks }}</ref> Head coach Ken Whisenhunt officially named Rolle the starting free safety to begin the regular season, along with strong safety [[Adrian Wilson (American football)|Adrian Wilson]].

On November 2, 2008, Rolle recorded four solo tackles, deflected a pass, and returned an interception by [[Marc Bulger]] for a 40-yard touchdown during the second quarter of a 34–13 win at the [[2008 St. Louis Rams|St. Louis Rams]] in Week 9.<ref name="stats8"/> In Week 16, he collected a season-high ten solo tackles in the Cardinals' 47–7 loss at the [[2008 New England Patriots|New England Patriots]].<ref name="stats8"/> In his first season as a free safety, Rolle recorded 89 combined tackles (78 solo), five passes defensed, an interception, and a touchdown in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref name="career"/>

The [[2008 Arizona Cardinals|Arizona Cardinals]] finished first in the [[NFC West]] with a 9–7 record and earned a wildcard berth. On January 3, 2009, Rolle started in his first career playoff game and recorded three combined tackles during a 30–24 victory against the [[2008 Atlanta Falcons|Atlanta Falcons]] in the NFC Wildcard Game.<ref name="stats8"/> The following week, he collected six combined tackles, deflected a pass, and intercepted a pass by [[Jake Delhomme]] in the Cardinals' 33–13 win at the [[2008 Carolina Panthers|Carolina Panthers]] in the NFC Divisional Round.<ref name="stats8"/> The Cardinals reached the [[Super Bowl]] after defeating the [[2008 Philadelphia Eagles|Philadelphia Eagles]] 32–25 in the [[NFC Championship Game]].<ref name="stats8"/> On February 1, 2009, Rolle started in [[Super Bowl XLIII]] and recorded three combined tackles as the Cardinals lost 27–23 in a closely contested matchup against the [[2008 Pittsburgh Steelers|Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref name="stats8">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antrel Rolle (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antrelrolle/2506347/gamelogs?season=2008 |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2009====
On February 9, 2009, head coach Ken Whisenhunt fired defensive coordinator Clancy Pendergast after he was the Cardinals' defensive coordinator for the last six seasons.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cards oust D-coordinator Pendergast |url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3891143 |access-date=June 4, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |date=February 9, 2009}}</ref> Their new defensive coordinator, [[Billy Davis (American football coach)|Bill Davis]], retained Rolle and Adrian Wilson as the starting safety tandem to start the 2009 regular season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Arizona Cardinals Depth Chart: 09/06/2009 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/40/ARZ |access-date=June 8, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

He started in the [[2009 Arizona Cardinals|Arizona Cardinals']] season-opener against the [[2009 San Francisco 49ers|San Francisco 49ers]] and recorded one tackle and a strip/sack in their 20–16 loss. His forced fumble on quarterback [[Shaun Hill]] was recovered by linebacker [[Bertrand Berry]] and marked the first sack of his career.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 1-2009: San Francisco 49ers @ Arizona Cardinals |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2009091309/2009/REG1/49ers@cardinals#tab=recap |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On October 25, 2009, he collected eight combined tackles, deflected a pass, and made an interception off a pass by [[Eli Manning]] during a 24–17 win at the [[2009 New York Giants|New York Giants]].<ref name="stats9"/> In Week 10, he collected a season-high nine solo tackles, made two pass deflections, and an interception in the Cardinals' 31–20 victory against the [[2009 Seattle Seahawks|Seattle Seahawks]].<ref name="stats9"/> On December 29, 2009, Rolle was voted to play in the [[2010 Pro Bowl]] to mark the first [[Pro Bowl]] selection of his career.<ref>{{cite web |title= 3 Pro Bowl picks show Arizona defense's growth |url= https://www.twincities.com/2009/12/31/3-pro-bowl-picks-show-arizona-defenses-growth/ |access-date= June 7, 2018 |website= TwinCities.com |publisher= Pioneer Press |date= December 31, 2009}}</ref> Head coach Ken Whisenhunt chose to rest Rolle during a Week 17 loss to the [[2009 Green Bay Packers|Green Bay Packers]] as the Cardinals had already clinched both a playoff berth and NFC West title with a 10–5 record prior to the game.<ref name="stats9"/> He completed the [[2009 NFL season|2009 season]] with 72 combined tackles (61 solo), eight passes defensed, four interceptions, and 1.5 sacks in 15 games and 15 starts. He also had one pass for nine-yards and returned six punts for 55-yards (9.2 YPR).<ref name="career"/>

On January 10, 2010, Rolle recorded a season-high 13 combined tackles (nine solo) during a 51–45 victory against the [[2009 Green Bay Packers|Green Bay Packers]] in the NFC Wildcard Game.<ref name="stats9"/> The following week, he made three combined tackles as the Cardinals were routed by the [[2009 New Orleans Saints|New Orleans Saints]] and lost 45–14 in the NFC Divisional Round.<ref name="stats9">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antrel Rolle (2009) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antrelrolle/2506347/gamelogs?season=2009 |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2010====
On March 4, 2010, the Arizona Cardinals released Rolle in order to avoid a $4 million roster bonus. General manager [[Rod Graves]] stated that team would be interested in re-signing Rolle.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cardinals drop starting safety Rolle |url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=4966290 |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=espn.com |agency=Associated Press |date=March 5, 2010}}</ref> Rolle immediately became an [[unrestricted free agent]] and attended meetings with the New York Giants and [[Miami Dolphins]]. The Miami Dolphins reportedly offered Rolle a five-year contract worth anywhere from $30-$35 million.<ref>{{cite web |title=2010 NFL Free Agency: Dolphins Make Offer to Antrel Rolle, Release Gibril Wilson |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/357255-nfl-free-agency-dolphins-make-offer-to-antrel-rolle-release-wilson |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=BleacherReport.com |author=Pinto, Michael |date=March 5, 2010}}</ref> He was ranked 68th by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2011]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2011-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On March 5, 2010, the [[New York Giants]] signed Rolle to a five-year, $37 million contract that includes $15 million guaranteed. The deal made Rolle the highest paid safety in league history.<ref>{{cite web |title=Former 'Canes star Antrel Rolle: "Show Me the Money," Dolphins: "No" |url=http://www.miaminewtimes.com/news/former-canes-star-antrel-rolle-show-me-the-money-dolphins-no-6524105 |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=miaminewtimes.com |date=March 8, 2010}}</ref>

Head coach [[Tom Coughlin]] named Rolle the starting free safety to begin the 2010 regular season, alongside strong safety [[Deon Grant]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: New York Giants Depth Chart: 09/02/2010 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/111/NYG |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> He started in the [[2010 New York Giants|New York Giants']] season-opener against the [[2010 Carolina Panthers|Carolina Panthers]] and collected a season-high eight combined tackles in their 31–18 victory. The following week, he tied his season-high of eight combined tackles during a 38–14 loss at the [[2010 Indianapolis Colts|Indianapolis Colts]] in Week 2. On October 17, 2010, Rolle recorded six combined tackles, broke up a pass, and made his first interception as a member of the Giants during a 28–20 victory against the [[2010 Detroit Lions|Detroit Lions]] in Week 6.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antrel Rolle (2010) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antrelrolle/2506347/gamelogs?season=2010 |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On December 28, 2010, Rolle was selected to play in the [[2011 Pro Bowl]], which marked his second consecutive selection.<ref>{{cite web |title=Four Giants selected to 2011 Pro Bowl, six players picked as alternate |url=http://www.nj.com/giants/index.ssf/2010/12/four_giants_selected_to_2011_p.html |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=nj.com |author=Berman, Zach |date=December 28, 2010}}</ref> He finished the [[2010 NFL season]] with 87 combined tackles (75 solo), four pass deflections, and an interception in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref name="career"/>

====2011====
Defensive coordinator [[Perry Fewell]] retained Rolle as the starting free safety in 2011, along with strong safety [[Kenny Phillips]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: New York Giants Depth Chart: 09/04/2011 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/123/NYG |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On September 19, 2011, Rolle collected a season-high nine combined tackles in the Giants' 28–16 victory against the [[2011 St. Louis Rams|St. Louis Rams]].<ref name="stats11"/> In Week 17, he recorded eight combined tackles, a pass deflection, and an interception during a 31–14 win against the [[2011 Dallas Cowboys|Dallas Cowboys]].<ref name="stats11"/> He finished the season with 96 combined tackles (82 solo), four pass deflections, and two interceptions in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref name="career"/> Rolle was required to play in the box and cover the slot receiver during the 2011 season.<ref name="nickel">{{cite web |title= Giants' added depth gives Antrel Rolle free safety spot he wants |url= https://www.newsday.com/sports/football/giants/giants-added-depth-gives-antrel-rolle-free-safety-spot-he-wants-v52303 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130825033943/http://www.newsday.com/sports/football/giants/giants-added-depth-gives-antrel-rolle-free-safety-spot-he-wants-1.5852212 |url-status= live |archive-date= August 25, 2013 |access-date= June 10, 2018 |website= newsday.com |date= August 7, 2013}}</ref>

The [[2011 New York Giants|New York Giants]] finished atop The [[NFC East]] with a 9–7 record and clinched a wildcard berth. On January 8, 2012, Rolle recorded nine combined tackles as the Giants routed the [[2011 Atlanta Falcons|Atlanta Falcons]] 24–2 in the NFC Wild Card Game.<ref name="stats11"/> They reached the [[Super Bowl]] after defeating the [[2011 Green Bay Packers|Green Bay Packers]] 37–20 in the NFC Divisional Round and the [[2011 San Francisco 49ers|San Francisco 49ers]] 20–17 in the [[NFC Championship Game]].<ref name="stats11">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antrel Rolle (2011) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antrelrolle/2506347/gamelogs?season=2011 |access-date=June 7, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On February 5, 2012, Rolle recorded three solo tackles as the New York Giants defeated the [[2011 New England Patriots|New England Patriots]] 21–17 to win [[Super Bowl XLVI]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201202050nwe.htm |title=Super Bowl XLVI - New York Giants vs. New England Patriots - February 5th, 2012 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=December 6, 2017}}</ref>

====2012====
Rolle and Kenny Phillips returned as the starting safety duo under head coach Tom Coughlin in 2012.<ref>{{cite web |title=New York Giants Depth Chart: Season-Opening Edition |url=https://www.bigblueview.com/2012/9/3/3288571/new-york-giants-depth-chart-season-opening-edition |access-date=June 10, 2018 |website=bigblueview.com |author=Valentine, Ed |date=September 3, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: New York Giants Depth Chart: 09/01/2012 |access-date=June 8, 2018 |url=http://Ourlads.com}}</ref> He started in the [[2012 New York Giants|New York Giants']] season-opener against the [[2012 Dallas Cowboys|Dallas Cowboys]] and collected a season-high nine solo tackles in their 24–17 loss.<ref name="stats12"/> On October 14, 2012, Rolle recorded six combined tackles, two pass deflections, and intercepted two passes by quarterback [[Alex Smith]] during a 26–3 victory at the [[2012 San Francisco 49ers|San Francisco 49ers]] in Week 6.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 6-2012: New York Giants @ San Francisco 49ers |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2012101409/2012/REG6/giants@49ers |access-date=June 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> This became Rolle's first multi-interception game since [[2007 NFL season|2007]]. In Week 13, he collected a season-high 11 combined tackles (five solo) in the Giants' 17–16 loss at the [[2012 Washington Redskins|Washington Redskins]].<ref name="stats12">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antrel Rolle (2012) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antrelrolle/2506347/gamelogs?season=2012 |access-date=June 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He completed the [[2012 NFL season|2012 season]] with 96 combined tackles (73 solo), five pass deflections, two interceptions, and a forced fumble in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref name="career"/> Although Rolle was the Giants' free safety, he was given nickelback duties and was required to play in the box and cover the slot.<ref name="nickel"/>

====2013====
Rolle entered training camp slated as the starting free safety after the Giants added depth and signed [[Aaron Ross]], [[Terell Thomas]], and [[Jayron Hosley]]. Strong safety [[Stevie Brown]] tore his ACL during camp and was slated to miss the entire season.<ref name="nickel"/> During the Giants second preseason game he sustained a sprained ankle. [[Ryan Mundy]] excelled at free safety during Rolle's two-game absence and was able to supplant Rolle as the starter.<ref>{{cite web |title= Signed as Depth, Mundy Looms Larger for Giants |url= https://nytimes.com/2013/09/08/sports/football/signed-as-depth-mundy-looms-larger-for-giants.html |access-date= June 10, 2018 |website= [[The New York Times]] |author= Pedulla, Tom |date= September 7, 2013}}</ref> Head coach Tom Coughlin officially named Rolle the starting strong safety to begin the regular season, alongside Mundy.<ref>{{cite web |title=New York Giants Roster 2013: Latest Cuts, Depth Charts and Analysis |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1750513-new-york-giants-roster-2013-latest-cuts-depth-charts-and-analysis#slide3 |access-date=June 10, 2018 |website=BleacherReport.com |author=Gagnon, Brad |date=August 26, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: New York Giants Depth Chart: 09/05/2013 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/150/NYG |access-date=June 10, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

On October 21, 2013, Rolle made a season-high three pass deflections, six combined tackles, and an interception during a 23–7 win against the [[2013 Minnesota Vikings|Minnesota Vikings]] in Week 7. In Week 10, he collected a season-high 12 combined tackles (ten solo) and a sack in the Giants' 24–20 win against the [[2013 Oakland Raiders|Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antrel Rolle (2013) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antrelrolle/2506347/gamelogs?season=2013 |access-date=June 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On December 15, 2013, Rolle recorded seven combined tackles, a pass deflection, and intercepted a pass by [[Russell Wilson]] during a 23–0 loss to the [[2013 Seattle Seahawks|Seattle Seahawks]] in Week 15.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 15-2013: Seattle Seahawks @ New York Giants |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013121506/2013/REG15/seahawks@giants |access-date=June 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On December 28, 2013, Rolle was named as an alternate to the [[2014 Pro Bowl]]. Rolle finished the [[2013 NFL season|2013 season]] with a 98 combined tackles (80 solo), 12 pass deflections, six interceptions, and two sacks in 16 games and 16 starts. He set career-highs in a four statistical categories.<ref name="career"/>

On January 20, 2014, it was announced that Rolle would play in the 2014 Pro Bowl as a late replacement for [[Earl Thomas (defensive back)|Earl Thomas]] who was appearing in the [[Super Bowl XLVIII]] with the [[2013 Seattle Seahawks|Seattle Seahawks]].<ref name="f456">{{cite web | last=Vacchiano | first=Ralph | title=Giants safety Antrel Rolle headed to Pro Bowl as replacement for Seattle’s Earl Thomas | website=New York Daily News | date=2014-01-20 | url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2014/01/20/giants-safety-antrel-rolle-headed-to-pro-bowl-as-replacement-for-seattles-earl-thomas/ | access-date=2024-09-23}}</ref> On January 24, 2014, he appeared in the 2014 Pro Bowl with [[Jerry Rice|Team Rice]] and helped them defeat [[Deion Sanders|Team Sanders]] 22–21.

====2014====
Defensive coordinator Perry Fewell chose to retain Rolle as the starting strong safety after he earned a Pro Bowl selection the previous season. He was officially named the starter to begin the regular season, opposite free safety [[Stevie Brown]].<ref>{{cite web |title=New York Giants release 2014 depth chart |url=https://www.bigblueview.com/2014/9/1/6090803/new-york-giants-2014-depth-chart |access-date=June 10, 2018 |website=bigblueview.com |author=Valentine, Ed |date=September 1, 2014}}</ref> In Week 5, Rolle collected a season-high 11 combined tackles (eight solo) in the Giants' 30–20 victory against the [[2014 Atlanta Falcons|Atlanta Falcons]]. The following week, he recorded four solo tackles, a pass deflection, and an interception during a 27–0 loss at the [[2014 Philadelphia Eagles|Philadelphia Eagles]] in Week 6.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antrel Rolle (2014) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antrelrolle/2506347/gamelogs?season=2014 |access-date=June 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He completed the season with 87 combined tackles (71 solo), nine passes defensed, three interceptions, and a forced fumble in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref name="career"/>

===Chicago Bears===
On March 11, 2015, the [[Chicago Bears]] signed Rolle to a three-year, $11.25 million contract with $4.90 million guaranteed.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Butt |first1=Jason |title=Bears sign S Antrel Rolle to three-year deal |url=http://fantasynews.cbssports.com/fantasyfootball/update/25103457/report-bears-agree-to-terms-with-s-antrel-rolle |publisher=CBSSports |access-date=March 12, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150314211056/http://fantasynews.cbssports.com/fantasyfootball/update/25103457/report-bears-agree-to-terms-with-s-antrel-rolle |archive-date=March 14, 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-ink-free-agents-Royal-Rolle/9ded44c1-c158-4bc9-b545-7420c37bdd30|title=Bears ink free agents Royal, Rolle|first=Larry|last=Mayer|work=ChicagoBears.com|date=March 11, 2015|access-date=March 12, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150313231520/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-ink-free-agents-Royal-Rolle/9ded44c1-c158-4bc9-b545-7420c37bdd30|archive-date=March 13, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Throughout training camp, Rolle competed to be the starting strong safety against former New York Giants' teammate Ryan Mundy. Head coach [[John Fox (American football)|John Fox]] named Rolle the starting strong safety to start the regular season, alongside free safety [[Brock Vereen]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Chicago Bears Depth Chart: 09/01/2015 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/175/CHI |access-date=June 10, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On September 27, 2015, Rolle collected a season-high ten combined tackles (seven solo) during a 26–0 loss at the [[2015 Seattle Seahawks|Seattle Seahawks]] in Week 3. The following week, he sustained an ankle injury during a 22–20 victory against the [[2015 Oakland Raiders|Oakland Raiders]] and was carted off the field in the second quarter. He was diagnosed with a sprained ankle and was sidelined for the next two games (Weeks 5–6).<ref>{{cite web |title=Antrel Rolle Injury: Updates on Bears Safety's Ankle and Return |url=https://www.bleacherreport.com/2575614-antrel-rolle-injury-updates-on-bears-safetys-ankle-and-return.html |access-date=June 10, 2018 |website=bleacherreport.com |author=Conway, Tyler |date=October 4, 2015 }}{{dead link|date=May 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> The injury snapped his 84-game streak of consecutive starts and also marked the first time he missed a game due to injury since his rookie season. On November 21, 2015, Rolle sustained a sprained MCL while participating in a walk-through during practice.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bears safety Antrel Rolle injured knee in Saturday's walk-through |url=https://www.bearswire.usatoday.com/2015/11/23/bears-safety-antrel-rolle-injured-knee-in-saturdays-walk-through/ |access-date=June 10, 2018 |website=bearswire.usatoday.com |author=Korman, Joey |date=November 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151225173737/http://bearswire.usatoday.com/2015/11/23/bears-safety-antrel-rolle-injured-knee-in-saturdays-walk-through/ |archive-date=December 25, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
On December 14, 2015, the Chicago Bears placed Rolle on [[injured reserve]] for the last three games of the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Bears put Rolle on IR with knee injury|url = http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-put-Rolle-on-IR-with-knee-injury/1c3eb4f5-d86e-4ccf-8f7d-0f82c1808e9d|website = www.chicagobears.com|access-date = December 16, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151216224719/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-put-Rolle-on-IR-with-knee-injury/1c3eb4f5-d86e-4ccf-8f7d-0f82c1808e9d|archive-date = December 16, 2015|url-status = dead}}</ref> He finished his lone season with the Chicago Bears with only 35 combined tackles (30 solo) and a pass deflection in seven games and seven starts.<ref name="career"/>

On May 1, 2016, the Chicago Bears released Rolle with two years remaining on his contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/chicago-bears-release-veteran-safety-antrel-rolle-0ap3000000659281|title=Chicago Bears release veteran safety Antrel Rolle|website=NFL.com|access-date=May 2, 2016}}</ref>

===Retirement===

'''Anttaj Hawthorne''' (born November 15, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive lineman]] for the [[Oakland Raiders]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin Badgers]], and was selected by the Raiders in the sixth round of the [[2005 NFL draft]]. Hawthorne also played for the [[Arizona Rattlers]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL).

==Early life==
Hawthorne attended [[Hamden High School]] in [[Hamden, Connecticut]], his hometown. He played on the varsity football team all four years of his high school career and was a member of the 2000 New Haven Register All-State football team.<ref>[http://www.iwasallstate.com/FallSports/Football/FootballAllStateTeams/2000s/2000/tabid/116/Default.aspx 2000 New Haven Register All-State football team]</ref> He got a scholarship to the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].  Anttaj participated in the first ever [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]] game on December 30, 2000.

==College career==
Hawthorne starred at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] for four years.  He was a team leader and a standout player.  Originally a Nose-tackle in his freshman year, later moved to left defensive tackle where he started 41 consecutive games.  Earned third-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors during his senior year and was also named All-Big Ten Conference three times, including a first-team selection as a junior, and a consensus selection as a senior.  His senior year, he was named team captain and later received the team's Jay Seiler Coaches Appreciation Award.  He finished his college career with a total of 201 tackles, 42 of which for a loss, 12 quarterback sacks, 2 forced fumbles, and 1 interception.  Currently 6th place on Wisconsin–Madison's all-time list with 42 tackles for a loss.

==Professional career==

===Oakland Raiders===
Hawthorne was selected by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the sixth round of the [[2005 NFL draft]] with the 175th overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2005 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2005/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-07 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He spent most of the 2005 season on the Raiders practice squad before finally being signed to the active roster on December 2. He was active for two games his first season, registering two assists in the Raiders regular season finale against the Giants.

In March 2006, he was allocated by the Raiders to the [[Frankfurt Galaxy (NFL Europe)|Frankfurt Galaxy]] of the [[NFL Europe]], where he helped the team win their fourth [[World Bowl]].

Hawthorne appeared in all 16 games for the Raiders in 2006, recording 13 tackles. He was waived by the team on September 1, 2007.

===Arizona Rattlers===
Hawthorne signed with the [[Arizona Rattlers]] of the [[Arena Football League]] in 2008, recording nine tackles, a sack and a fumble recovery during his rookie season. On August 10, 2012, Hawthorne and the Rattlers won [[ArenaBowl XXV]] over the [[Philadelphia Soul]] one year after losing [[ArenaBowl XXIV]] to the [[Jacksonville Sharks]]. The Rattlers returned to a 3rd straight [[ArenaBowl]] in [[ArenaBowl XXVI|2013]], defeating the Soul once again.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2013/08/17/arenabowl-xxvi-rattlers-win-2nd-arena-football-league-title-in-row/ |title=ArenaBowl XXVI: Rattlers win 2nd Arena Football League title in row |date=August 17, 2013 |author=Joe Williams |publisher=Orlando Sentinel |work=www.orlandosentinel.com |access-date=August 19, 2013}}</ref> On March 9, 2016, Hawthorne was assigned to the Rattlers.

'''Antwan Deon Odom''' (born September 24, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]] and was selected by the [[Tennessee Titans]] in the second round of the [[2004 NFL draft]]. Odom also played for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].

He went to high school at [[Alma Bryant High School]], where he started at defensive end and occasionally played wide receiver.

==College career==
Odom played in 39 games for the [[University of Alabama]] during his five-year collegiate career. He recorded 98 tackles, 21 sacks, and 26 tackles for losses in his career.

As a freshman, Odom played in every game with two starts. He was named an honorable mention for Freshman [[All-American]] by [[Rivals.com]]. As a sophomore, Odom's season was ended after receiving and having surgery on a torn [[Glenoid labrum|labrum]] in his left shoulder and met requirement to regain a year of eligibility by the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]].

During his redshirt sophomore year, he played in all 13 games for the Tide and recorded 42 tackles with 10 sacks.

His junior season, Odom was named as [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] after starting every game of the season at right defensive end in which he recorded 40 [[Tackles for loss|tackles]], 8 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]], and 9.5 tackles for loss. He was later honored with the team's Dwight Stephenson Most Valuable Lineman Award.

On April 14, 2010, Antwan was selected to the University of Alabama's "Team of the Decade". An Alabama Team of the Decade has been selected by Crimson Tide fans since originated by Alabama Sports Information Director Charley Thornton in 1970. The teams have been selected by readers of 'BAMA Magazine and BamaMag.com the past four decades.

==Professional career==

===Tennessee Titans===
Odom was selected in the second round of the 2004 NFL draft, as the 57th overall and 3rd pick by the Tennessee Titans.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2004/draft.htm |title=2004 NFL Draft Listing |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=2023-05-06}}</ref> He played four seasons with the Titans as he was a key defensive lineman during the Titans' [[2008 Tennessee Titans season|2007-08 season]] in which he recorded some of his best career numbers to date. Coming in second on the team to [[Kyle Vanden Bosch]], Odom recorded 8.0 sacks on the season <ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.nfl.com/teams/tennesseetitans/statistics?season=2007&team=TEN&seasonType=| title=Tennessee Titans Stats| work=NFL.com| access-date=March 4, 2008| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080307034420/http://www.nfl.com/teams/tennesseetitans/statistics?season=2007&team=TEN&seasonType=| archive-date= March 7, 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref> including 2.0 which helped the Titans defeat the Colts in Week 17 and make the [[NFL Playoffs|playoffs]] for the first time since the [[2003 NFL season|2003 season]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.nfl.com/players/antwanodom/gamelogs?id=ODO051141| title=Antwan Odom: Game Logs| work=NFL.com| access-date=March 4, 2008| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080307024203/http://www.nfl.com/players/antwanodom/gamelogs?id=ODO051141| archive-date= March 7, 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
He was signed by the Cincinnati Bengals during [[Free agent|free agency]] in 2008,<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.bengals.com/news/news.asp?story_id=6670| title=Odom's first Bengal sack| first=Geoff|last= Hobson| publisher=Bengals.com| date=March 3, 2008| access-date=March 3, 2008| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080305192902/http://www.bengals.com/news/news.asp?story_id=6670| archive-date= March 5, 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref> after becoming one of fourteen free agents from the Titans.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.tennessean.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20080214/SPORTS01/802140395/1027/RSS0201| title=Odom gives Titans shot to keep him| first=Jim|last= Wyatt| newspaper=The Tennessean| date=February 14, 2008| access-date= March 4, 2008}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref> Odom suffered two injuries that caused him to miss time in 2008.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.bengals.com/team/roster/Antwan-Odom/47c696ff-c517-43f4-abc2-54629cc183a4| title=Antwan Odom| publisher=Bengals.com| access-date=March 25, 2009| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090502215146/http://www.bengals.com/team/roster/Antwan-Odom/47c696ff-c517-43f4-abc2-54629cc183a4| archive-date= May 2, 2009 | url-status= live}}</ref> He missed the entire preseason schedule due to foot injury suffered in opening training camp practice on July 28. He was inactive for four games due to a shoulder injury suffered in practice. In the second week of the 2009 regular season, Odom tied a Bengals franchise record by sacking quarterback [[Aaron Rodgers]] five times in a 31–24 win over the [[Green Bay Packers]]. Odom left the Week 6 game versus the Texans with an [[Achilles heel]] injury. ESPN reported that Odom would be out for the season. Before Training Camp, Odom was quoted in saying he was ready for the 2010 season, as he said the tendon was feeling better and he could run and be ready to play and start at 100%.

On July 29, 2011, Odom was released by the Bengals.<ref>{{cite web | last=Walker | first=James | title=Bengals release DE Antwan Odom | website=ESPN.com | date=2011-07-29 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/post/_/id/42413/bengals-release-de-antwan-odom | access-date=2025-07-26}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In his spare time, Odom enjoys fishing and hunting. He is also a NASCAR racing and pro-wrestling enthusiast. Odom earned a degree in Human Environmental Studies upon completing his course work at the University of Alabama.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://antwanodom98.com/about-antwan/biography.html|title= About Antwan|work= Antwan Odom 98|access-date= July 23, 2012|date= 2010|url-status= dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120305185511/http://antwanodom98.com/about-antwan/biography.html|archive-date= March 5, 2012}}</ref>

On March 15, 2011, Odom's home in [[Mason, OH]] (a suburb of [[Cincinnati]]) was severely damaged by fire.
Odom and his family were safe at his family's house in Cordova, Alabama at the time.<ref>{{cite news |title=Fire damages home of Cincinnati Bengals player Antwan Odom |first1= Joe |last1=Reedy|first2=Janice|last2= Morse |url=http://news.cincinnati.com/article/20110315/NEWS01/303150042/Fire-damages-home-Cincinnati-Bengals-player-Antwan-Odom |newspaper=Cincinnati Enquirer |date=March 15, 2011 |access-date=March 15, 2011}}</ref> On August 22, 2011, Odom was shot in the leg at his home in Irvington.<ref name="arrested">{{cite news|url=http://blog.al.com/live/2011/12/former_nfl_defensive_lineman_o.html|title=Former NFL defensive lineman Antwan Odom arrested on marijuana charge|last=Kent|first=Mark R.|date=December 15, 2011|publisher=Al.com|newspaper=Alabama Press-Register|access-date=April 13, 2012}}</ref> Odom was arrested on December 15, 2011, for possession of marijuana after a traffic stop in Baldwin County, Alabama. He was released later in the day after posting $1,000.00 bail.<ref name="arrested"/>

Odom was charged with one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and health care fraud, one count of wire fraud, and one count of health care fraud by the [[United States Department of Justice]] on July 24, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Six Former NFL Players Charged in Superseding Indictment Alleging Nationwide Fraud on Health Care Benefit Program for Retired NFL Players |url=https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/six-former-nfl-players-charged-superseding-indictment-alleging-nationwide-fraud-health-care |website=Justice.gov |date=July 24, 2020 |access-date=January 2, 2021}}</ref> He pleaded guilty by December 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Estep, Bill |title=With latest plea, a dozen former NFL players have admitted guilt in KY fraud case |url=https://www.kentucky.com/news/local/crime/article247524200.html |website=Kentucky.com |date=December 1, 2020 |access-date=January 2, 2021}}</ref> By February 2022, he had been sentenced to 180 days of [[house arrest]] and ordered to perform 240 hours of community service.<ref>{{cite news |title=Former NFL Player Sentenced to Prison for Nationwide Health Care Fraud Scheme |url=https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/former-nfl-player-sentenced-prison-nationwide-health-care-fraud-scheme |website=Justice.gov |date=February 9, 2022 |access-date=May 12, 2022}}</ref>

'''Antwain Joquan Spann''' (born February 22, 1983) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] for the [[New England Patriots]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[New York Giants]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2005. He played [[college football]] for the [[Louisiana–Lafayette Ragin' Cajuns football|Louisiana–Lafayette Ragin' Cajuns]].

Spann was also a member of the [[Rhein Fire (NFL Europe)|Rhein Fire]], [[Buffalo Bills]], [[Denver Broncos]], and [[Florida Tuskers]].

==Early life==
Spann played football at [[El Camino High School (Oceanside)|El Camino High School]] in [[Oceanside, California]].

==College career==
Spann began his college football career in 2001 at [[Mississippi Gulf Coast Community College]], where he was a Mississippi Junior College All-State and All-Region player. In 2003, he transferred to the [[University of Louisiana at Lafayette]], where he started 11 games at cornerback in his senior season in 2004, recording a team-high four interceptions.

==Professional career==
===New York Giants===
Spann was signed by the Giants as an undrafted free agent on May 17, 2005, following the [[2005 NFL draft]]. He was waived by the Giants on August 31.

===New England Patriots===
Spann was signed to the Patriots' practice squad on January 2, 2006, where he spent the remainder of the team's postseason before being signed to a future contract by the team on January 17.

Spann was waived by the team on September 2, 2006, and signed to the Patriots' practice squad the following day. He was signed to the Patriots' 53-man roster on September 30 before being waived from it on November 7. He was re-signed to the Patriots' practice squad on November 8, and again elevated to the 53-man roster on November 18. He was waived by the Patriots on November 22 and re-signed to their practice squad again on November 24. He was signed to the team's 53-man roster for a third time on December 9, where he spent the remainder of the season.

Spann was waived by the team on July 19, 2007, and signed to the Patriots' practice squad on September 25. He then was signed to the Patriots' 53-man roster on December 28.

Spann was waived by the Patriots again on August 30, 2008, and signed to the team's practice squad on September 1. He was elevated to the 53-man roster on October 22 when [[Safety (American football position)|safety]] [[Rodney Harrison]] was placed on [[injured reserve]].

Spann was waived by the Patriots on July 27, 2009, after signing 2009 draft pick [[Patrick Chung]].

===Buffalo Bills===
Spann signed with the [[Buffalo Bills]] on July 31, 2009. He was briefly waived on August 7 before being re-signed on August 11. He was waived again on August 21 when [[2009 NFL draft|2009]] first-round pick [[Aaron Maybin]] was signed.

===Denver Broncos===
Spann was claimed off waivers by the [[Denver Broncos]] on August 24, 2009. He was waived on September 5.

'''Antonio Perkins'''  (born January 9, 1982) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[kick returner]] and [[cornerback]] for two seasons with the [[Cleveland Browns]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) during the early 2000s.  He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]], earning [[unanimous All-American]] honors.  Perkins was selected by the Browns in the fourth round of the [[2005 NFL draft]].

== Early life ==
Perkins was born in [[Lawton, Oklahoma]].  He attended [[Lawton High School]], graduating in 2000.  He was a [[Letterman (sports)|letterman]] in football, basketball and track.

== College career ==
Perkins attended the [[University of Oklahoma]], and played for coach [[Bob Stoops]]'s [[Oklahoma Sooners football]] team from 2000 to 2004.  In 47 games with the Sooners, he started 30 times and finished with 125 tackles, one sack, five stops for losses, two forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries and 21 pass deflections.  He set the [[NCAA]] record for most punt returns for touchdowns in a single game, with three, as well as most punt return yards in a game with 277, against [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA]] in 2003.  He is tied with [[Wes Welker]] and [[Ted Ginn Jr.]] for second most punt return touchdowns in a career with eight second to [[Dante Pettis]] of the [[Washington Huskies]] who has nine.  As a junior in 2003, he was a first-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] selection, and was recognized as a [[unanimous All-American]].<ref>''2011 NCAA Football Records Book'', [http://fs.ncaa.org/Docs/stats/football_records/2011/Awards.pdf  Award Winners], National Collegiate Athletic Association, Indianapolis, Indiana, p. 11 (2011).  Retrieved June 26, 2012.</ref>

== Professional career ==
Perkins was drafted in the fourth round, 103rd overall, by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the [[2005 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2005 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2005/draft.htm |access-date=May 7, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played in one game in 2005 and activated for five games in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Perkins Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PerkAn20.htm |access-date=2025-08-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  The Browns waived Perkins on October 28, 2006, but subsequently re-signed him and assigned him to their [[practice squad]]. In June 2007, Perkins was waived by Cleveland and claimed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] then released as a final training camp cut on September 1.<ref name="Argos profile">{{Cite web|url=http://www.argonauts.ca/Argos/Team/Roster/Antonio_Perkins.html |title=Antonio Perkins, cornerback |work=Roster |publisher=Toronto Argonauts Football Club |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080407021933/http://www.argonauts.ca/Argos/Team/Roster/Antonio_Perkins.html |archivedate=April 7, 2008 }}</ref>

On March 28, 2008, the Toronto Argonauts signed Perkins as a free agent.<ref name="Argos profile" />  He was subsequently released on June 14.

He helped the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Nittany Lions]] lead the conference in pass efficiency defense in 2005, and made 104 [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]] and seven [[interception]]s in his collegiate career. ===New Orleans Saints===
Phillips signed as an [[Undrafted sportsperson|undrafted]] [[free agent]] with the [[New Orleans Saints]] following the [[2006 NFL draft]]. '''Antonio Pittman''' (born December 19, 1985) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for the [[St. Louis Rams]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]]. After his football career, he became a [[firefighter]].

==Early life==
Pittman attended [[Buchtel High School]] in [[Akron, Ohio]], where he earned All-Ohio honors as a senior. Pittman majored in [[African American]] and [[African Studies]] at Ohio State. On Pittman's left arm is a tattoo honoring his brother, Anthony, who died at the age of 23.<ref name="helmet">{{cite press release
 |title=Under the Helmet with Antonio Pittman 
 |publisher=Ohio State Department of Athletics 
 |date=2006-09-23 
 |url=http://ohiostatebuckeyes.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/2006mag-psu-pittman.html 
 |access-date=2006-11-12 
}}{{dead link|date=July 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
While in high school Pittman lived with his sister.<ref name="helmet"/>
He has one daughter, Keilyn.

==College career==

===2005===
Despite a slow start to the 2005 season, he finished the year with 1,331 yards rushing and seven touchdowns on 243 carries.  His rushing yardage was the 10th-best single-season mark in school history and only Archie Griffin gained more yards (1,577) as a sophomore.<ref>[http://graphics.fansonly.com/photos/schools/osu/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/records.pdf Record Book (Part 1)] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930043915/http://graphics.fansonly.com/photos/schools/osu/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/records.pdf |date=2007-09-30 }}</ref> His rushing total was the 11th highest in the NCAA that season and 5th best in the [[Big Ten Conference]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/college-football/stats/player NCAA Division I-A Rushing Leaders]</ref> In addition to running, Pittman made 17 receptions for 161 yards in 2005.

In his first appearance, Pittman rushed for 100 yards on 14 carries against [[Miami University]].  His career-high is 186 yards in a game against the [[University of Minnesota]], where he also scored his first touchdown of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Pittman 2005 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/antonio-pittman-1/gamelog/2005 |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  He scored the winning touchdown in the 2005 game against the [[Michigan Wolverines]]. His run around the Michigan defensive line for a three-yard touchdown run came with just 24 seconds left in the game.<ref name="no bone"/> In the next game, he clinched the 2006 [[Tostitos Fiesta Bowl]] against the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish]] by erupting for a 60-yard touchdown run with 1:46 left in the game, despite having an injured hamstring.<ref name="no bone"/> In 2005, he became just the fourth sophomore in Ohio State annals to rush for 1,000 or more yards in a season, joining [[Archie Griffin]], [[Vince Workman]] and [[Keith Byars]].<ref name="no bone">{{cite news |first = Marla |last = Ridenour |title = No back bone to pick |url = http://www.ohio.com/mld/ohio/sports/colleges/ohio_state_university/15284737.htm |work= [[Akron Beacon Journal]] |date = 2006-08-16 |access-date = 2006-08-31}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref>

===2006===
[[Image:2006 09 09 Ohio State vs Texas.jpg|thumb|[[Troy Smith]] hands off to Pittman against [[2006 Texas Longhorns football team|Texas]]]]
In 2006, [[quarterback]] [[Troy Smith]] said of Pittman, "Everybody knows who he is in the state of Ohio, but I think nationally, he's one of the top three backs."<ref name="ground rules">{{cite news |first = Ken |last = Gordon |title = Ground Rules |url = http://www.dispatch.com/football/football.php?story=dispatch/2006/08/31/20060831-E1-00.html |work = [[Columbus Dispatch]] |date = 2006-08-31 |access-date = 2006-08-31 }}{{Dead link|date=September 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Pittman averaged more than five yards per carry in his three seasons, playing in 35 games, rushing for an average of 84 yards per game.<ref name="ncaa">{{cite web | title = Antonio Pittman Stats | work = DI Statistics | publisher = [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] | date = 2006-09-16 | url = http://web1.ncaa.org/d1mfb/playerDetail.jsp?yr=2006&org=518&player=25 | access-date = 2006-09-21}}</ref> He currently ranks 8th on Ohio State's all-time rushing list.

At the beginning of the 2006 season some called for split playing time between Pittman and freshman [[Chris Wells (American football)|Chris Wells]], another Akron native. However, Pittman's strong resume in 2005 and early successes guaranteed his role as starter.<ref>{{cite news|first=Terry |last=Pluto |title=Pittman well-suited for OSU |url=http://www.ohio.com/mld/ohio/sports/columnists/terry_pluto/15541501.htm |work=[[Akron Beacon Journal]] |date=2006-09-17 |access-date=2006-09-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061030182603/http://www.ohio.com/mld/ohio/sports/columnists/terry_pluto/15541501.htm |archive-date=2006-10-30 |url-status=live }}</ref>

As the starting running back, Pittman displayed the ability to compile impressive statistics. In games against [[Northern Illinois University|Northern Illinois]], [[University of Cincinnati|Cincinnati]], [[Penn State University|Penn State]], and [[University of Iowa|Iowa]] he rushed for over 100 yards and scored touchdowns. Also, during the game at then #2 [[Texas Longhorns|Texas]] he scored a touchdown. Against the [[Florida Gators]] in the [[BCS National Championship]], Pittman rushed for 62 yards and one of Ohio State's two scores. On January 15, 2007, Pittman made the decision to forgo his senior year and declared himself eligible for the [[NFL draft]].

Pittman was waived on September 5, 2009.

Pittman played for the [[Omaha Nighthawks]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.statscrew.com/football/stats/p-pittmant001 | title=Antonio Pittman | publisher=statscrew.com | accessdate=May 17, 2024}}</ref>

== Personal ==
On September 4, 2015, Pittman graduated from the Ohio Fire Academy with the intent of becoming a [[firefighter]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.myfox28columbus.com/news/features/top-stories/stories/Former-Buckeye-and-NFL-Player-Graduates-Fire-Academy-200113.shtml |title=Former Buckeye and NFL Player Graduates Fire Academy - WTTE - WTTE FOX28 |access-date=2015-09-13 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150914042653/http://www.myfox28columbus.com/news/features/top-stories/stories/Former-Buckeye-and-NFL-Player-Graduates-Fire-Academy-200113.shtml |archive-date=2015-09-14 }}</ref>  On December 14, 2017, he joined the [[Middletown, Ohio|Middletown]] Division of Fire.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.journal-news.com/news/middletown-newest-firefighters-include-former-nfl-player-city-native/aZXNGZq3Yi2DHlyYuepBYN/|title=Middletown's newest firefighters include former NFL player, city native|last=Richter|first=Ed|newspaper=Journal-News|date=December 14, 2017|access-date=December 15, 2017}}</ref> Pittman would later join the Columbus Division of Fire in 2020.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.10tv.com/article/former-ohio-state-running-back-antonio-pittman-becomes-columbus-firefighter-2020-feb|title=Former Ohio State running back Antonio Pittman becomes Columbus firefighter|last=Crisp|first=Lacey|publisher=WBNS-TV|date=February 17, 2020|access-date=February 18, 2020|archive-date=February 19, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200219002604/https://www.10tv.com/article/former-ohio-state-running-back-antonio-pittman-becomes-columbus-firefighter-2020-feb|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] for the [[University of Alabama]], and was recognized as an [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]]. Selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the first round of the [[1994 NFL draft]], Langham also played professionally for the [[Baltimore Ravens]], [[San Francisco 49ers]], and [[New England Patriots]] of the NFL. ==Early life== Langham was born in [[Town Creek, Alabama]]. He graduated from Hazlewood High School in Town Creek. ==College career== Langham attended the University of Alabama, where he played for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football]] team as a [[defensive back]] from 1990 to 1993. On the eventual [[1992 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|1992 national championship team]] Langham, in his sophomore year, returned an interception for a touchdown late in the 4th quarter of the [[1992 SEC Championship Game]]. As a junior in 1993, he was recognized as a consensus first-team All-American and would win the [[Jim Thorpe Award]] as the nation's top defensive back. Later, however, he caused the Crimson Tide to forfeit most of its [[1993 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|1993 season]] and suffer [[NCAA]] sanctions by signing with an agent during the previous offseason. Langham also signed and submitted an application to enter the [[1993 NFL draft]], rendering him ineligible under NCAA rules, regardless of whether he had signed with an agent or not. The Crimson Tide's head coach, [[Gene Stallings]], failed to inform both the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) and the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) of Langham's draft application, or to declare Langham ineligible as required by NCAA rules. His ineligibility was revealed in late November 1993 and the University of Alabama eventually had to forfeit eight wins and a tie from the 1993 season.{{cite web|url=https://goomer.ncaa.org/wdbctx/LSDBi/LSDBi.MajorInfPackage.ProcessMultipleBylaws?p_Multiple=0&p_PK=160&p_Button=View+Public+Report&p_TextTerms=ThisIsADummyPhraseThatWillNotBeDuplicated&p_TextTerms2=ThisIsADummyPhraseThatWillNotBeDuplicated&p_Division=1 |title=NCAA Public Report on Infractions at Alabama |access-date=December 11, 2006 }}{{dead link|date=July 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} He still holds the Crimson Tide's team record for career interceptions with 19.[http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/alab/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/record-book.pdf Record Book] cstv.com {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120916033456/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/alab/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/record-book.pdf |date=September 16, 2012 }} ==Professional career== {{NFL predraft | height ft = 5 | height in = 11 | weight = 180 | arm span = 32 | hand span = 8 7/8 }} The Cleveland Browns selected Langham in the first round (ninth pick overall) of the 1994 NFL draft, and he played for the Browns during the {{NFL Year|1994}} and {{NFL Year|1995}} seasons.{{Cite web |title=1994 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1994/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} He is one of three players to have played for the Cleveland Browns before they became the Baltimore Ravens and return to the Browns after the expansion team formed in 1999; the other players are [[Jerry Ball]] and [[Orlando Brown (American football, born 1970)|Orlando Brown]]. '''Antonio DeShonta Smith''' (born October 21, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma State Cowboys football|Oklahoma State Cowboys]], and was selected by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] in the fifth round of the [[2004 NFL draft]]. He also played for the [[Denver Broncos]], [[Oakland Raiders]], and the [[Houston Texans]] in the NFL and for the [[Hamburg Sea Devils (NFL Europe)|Hamburg Sea Devils]] of [[NFL Europe]]. Smith won [[Super Bowl 50]] as a member of the Broncos.

==College career==
Smith played [[college football]] at [[Oklahoma State Cowboys football|Oklahoma State]]. He was an honorable mention All-Big 12 in his junior season at Oklahoma State.<ref>{{cite web  | title=Oklahoma State Profile  | work=okstate.com  | url=http://www.okstate.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/070303aac.html  | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131206085332/http://www.okstate.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/070303aac.html  | archive-date=December 6, 2013  | url-status=dead  }}</ref>
Antonio played for NEO A&M College in Miami, Oklahoma during his freshman (2000) and sophomore (2001) season. He transferred to Oklahoma State for his junior (2002) and senior (2003) seasons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.neoathletics.com/sports/2012/10/30/FB_1030124737.aspx?path=football|title=NFL Norsemen}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
Smith was drafted in the fifth round with the 135th overall selection in the [[2004 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2004/draft.htm |title=2004 NFL Draft Listing |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=2023-05-06}}</ref> Following his rookie season, he played in the developmental NFL Europe as a member of the [[2005 Hamburg Sea Devils season|2005 Hamburg Sea Devils]].

During the [[2008 NFL season]], Smith played in every game and had 2 forced [[fumbles]] and 3.5 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]]. Smith helped the Cardinals reach [[Super Bowl XLIII]], but the team would lose 27–23 to the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. Despite a great performance during the course of the season, the Cardinals chose not to re-sign him and let him go into [[Free agent|free agency]].

===Houston Texans (first stint)===
Smith was signed as an [[unrestricted free agent]] by the [[Houston Texans]] to replace the released [[Anthony Weaver]].

In 2011, Smith went to his first career [[2012 Pro Bowl|Pro Bowl]], replacing the [[New England Patriots]]' [[Andre Carter]] who was unable to play due to injury.<ref>{{cite web | title= Texans C Myers, DE Smith added to Pro Bowl roster | work= abclocal.go.com | url= https://abc13.com/archive/8511838/ | access-date= January 19, 2012 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120218002922/http://abclocal.go.com/ktrk/story?section=news%2Fsports%2Fpro%2Ffootball&id=8511838 | archive-date= February 18, 2012 | url-status= live }}</ref>

In 2013, Smith was suspended for week one after an incident in the preseason in which he removed [[Miami Dolphins]] lineman [[Richie Incognito]]'s helmet and swung it at him.<ref>{{cite web|last=McIntyre|first=Brian|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nfl-shutdown-corner/report-texans-antonio-smith-suspended-week-1-helmet-174519695.html|title=Report: Texans DE Antonio Smith to be suspended for Week 1 after helmet swinging incident|publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|date=August 20, 2013|access-date=August 21, 2013}}</ref> On November 29, 2013, he was fined $15,750 for hitting [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]' quarterback [[Chad Henne]] in the head and neck region.

===Oakland Raiders===
On March 14, 2014, Smith signed a two-year, $9 million contract with the [[Oakland Raiders]] and played defensive tackle in the Raiders base 4-3 defense.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schefter |first=Adam |author-link=Adam Schefter |date=March 14, 2014 |title=Former Texans DE Antonio Smith just signed a 2-year, $9M deal with the Raiders. |url=https://twitter.com/AdamSchefter/status/444619349781798912 |access-date=March 14, 2014 |publisher=Twitter}}</ref> He was released by the Raiders on March 31, 2015.

===Denver Broncos===
On April 2, 2015, Smith signed a one-year, $2 million contract with the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Florio |first=Mike |author-link=Mike Florio |date=2015-04-02 |title=Antonio Smith lands with Broncos |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/antonio-smith-lands-with-broncos |access-date=2024-12-21 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

On February 7, 2016, Smith was part of the Broncos team that won Super Bowl 50. In the game, the Broncos defeated the [[2015 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]] by a score of 24–10.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201602070den.htm|title=Super Bowl 50 - Denver Broncos vs. Carolina Panthers - February 7th, 2016|work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|access-date=August 31, 2017}}</ref>

===Houston Texans (second stint)===
After initially deciding to retire following the Super Bowl victory, Smith was contacted by his former team, the Houston Texans, and decided to return for one more season.<ref name="l860">{{Cite web |date=2016-09-28 |title=Antonio Smith on new role and returning "home" |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/antonio-smith-on-new-role-and-returning-home-17784269 |access-date=2024-12-09 |website=Houston Texans}}</ref> On September 28, 2016, Smith was signed by the Texans.<ref>{{cite web|title=Texans sign DE Antonio Smith|url=http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-sign-DE-Antonio-Smith/19966996-26ab-4ae0-bf9c-b6bf7e8d5e84|website=HoustonTexans.com|access-date=September 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161002090346/http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-sign-DE-Antonio-Smith/19966996-26ab-4ae0-bf9c-b6bf7e8d5e84|archive-date=October 2, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> After the season, he would retire for good.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Antonio Smith: The Ninja's now a Rancher {{!}} Where are they Now? |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/antonio-smith-the-ninja-s-now-a-rancher-where-are-they-now |access-date=2024-05-08 |website=www.houstontexans.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Smith has three children, Antonio Smith Jr. (2003), Winter Smith (2009) and Marty Smith (2014).

Smith, along with his sister Antwonette, founded Smith's Little People With Big Challenges Foundation. The organization's mission is to fight childhood obesity.

Smith's father died 4 days before [[Super Bowl 50]], due to heart surgery complications.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.denverpost.com/broncos/ci_29469993/father-antonio-smith-broncos-dl-dies-after-complications|title=Father of Antonio Smith of Broncos dies after complications from heart surgery|work=The Denver Post|date=February 3, 2016|access-date=February 4, 2016|first=Mark|last=Kiszla}}</ref> Antonio Smith shares his knowledge and talent by volunteering his time as a defensive line coach for the Christian Heritage high school football team (Del City, OK). The team played in 2018 Oklahoma state class A champion state final.

Following his retirement, Smith returned to his native Oklahoma and became a [[ranch]]er, raising rabbits, horses, and cattle.<ref name=":0" />

'''Antwan Tabari Lake''' (born July 10, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[West Virginia Mountaineers football|West Virginia Mountaineers]] and was signed by the [[Detroit Lions]] of the NFL as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2002.

Lake also played for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] and [[New Orleans Saints]] of the NFL, and the [[Las Vegas Locomotives]] of the [[United Football League (2009–2012)|United Football League]].

==College career==
Antwan Lake enrolled at [[West Virginia University]] in 1998. He played outside linebacker his freshman season, recording 9 tackles, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery, and 3 sacks.

As a sophomore, in 1999, Lake shifted to [[defensive tackle]]. That season, he totaled 39 tackles and three sacks. As a junior, 2000, hr only recorded 13 tackles and one sack. In his final season, 2001, hr recorded 26 tackles and 3 sacks. In his career, the three-year starter totaled 87 tackles, 10 sacks, and 15 tackles-for-a-loss.

==Professional career==

===Detroit Lions===
After being undrafted in the [[2002 NFL draft]], Antwan Lake joined the [[Detroit Lions]]. He played in nine games as a rookie, recording two tackles.

===Atlanta Falcons===
After his rookie season with Detroit, Lake was signed by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] on December 21, 2003. He did not see playing time for the rest of the 2003 season.

In 2004, Lake played in every game on the season. He recorded 17 tackles and deflected a pass on the season.

In 2005, Antwan Lake recorded 21 tackles, 3.5 sacks, two forced fumbles, and a safety while playing in 13 games on the season.

===New Orleans Saints===
After being cut from Atlanta in 2005, Lake was picked up by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in 2006. He played in 15 games that season, totaling 15 tackles, one sack, and a pass deflection.

In 2007, Lake totaled 18 tackles, one sack, and four safeties.

'''Antwon Burton''' (born July 11, 1983) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[Denver Broncos]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2006. He played [[college football]] for the [[Temple Owls football|Temple Owls]].

Burton was also a member of the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], [[Kansas City Chiefs]], [[St. Louis Rams]], [[Carolina Panthers]], [[Florida Tuskers]], [[Sacramento Mountain Lions]] and [[Virginia Destroyers]].

==Early life==
Burton was a First-team All-State and All-Western New York selection as a senior at [[Cleveland Hill School District|Cleveland Hill]] High School in [[Cheektowaga, New York]].

==College career==
Burton played 22 games (16 starts) and totaled 96 tackles in two seasons at [[Temple University]] after transferring from [[Erie Community College]] in Orchard Park, N.Y. As a senior in 2005, Burton played 11 games (10 starts), posting 66 tackles (26 solo), five tackles-for-losses, four fumble recoveries, three forced fumbles and three pass breakups. Burton concluded his collegiate career by playing in the [[East-West Shrine Game]]. Before the start of his senior year, he was named one of the top five independent pro prospects by the [[College Football News]]. He played 11 games (6 starts) in his first year at Temple as a junior in 2003 before missing the 2004 season with a foot injury. He posted 6.5 sacks and was voted First-team All-Northeast Conference at [[Erie Community College]] in 2002.

==Professional career==

===Pre-draft===
At his pro day workout at Temple University, Burton measured 6-1{{frac|3|4}} and 308 pounds. He ran a 5.39 forty-yard dash and did 31 reps of 225 pounds. He also had a 31{{frac|1|2}}" vertical leap and a broad jump of 9'5"

===Denver Broncos===
Burton, who entered the NFL with the Broncos as a college free agent on May 3, 2006, was signed to Denver's practice squad after training camp. He was signed to the Broncos' active roster on November 12, 2006, and made his professional
debut with an assisted tackle at Oakland on November 12, 2006.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antwon Burton 2006 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BurtAn20/gamelog/2006/ |access-date=2024-03-22 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was declared inactive for the rest of the season. In 2007, he played in six games and made eight tackles (five solo). He was waived on November 13, 2007, and signed November 14, 2007 to Broncos practice squad, where he finished the season.

===Cincinnati Bengals===
Burton signed with Bengals as a free agent on May 4, 2008. Burton was on the roster of the Kansas City Chiefs and St. Louis Rams in 2008 but did not play in a game.

===Carolina Panthers===
Burton signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]] on September 22, 2009, after they lost [[Ma'ake Kemoeatu]] and [[Louis Leonard]] for the season. He was waived on October 20, after the Panthers acquired [[Tank Tyler]] from [[Kansas City Chiefs|Kansas City]].

'''Antuan Minye' Edwards''' (born May 26, 1977) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (American football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Edwards was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the first round (25th overall) of the [[1999 NFL draft]] out of [[Clemson University]].

==Early life and college==
He attended [[Starkville High School]] in Mississippi, where he played [[quarterback]], safety, and [[Running back (American football)|running back]]. He was named [[All-American]] as a safety in his [[Twelfth grade|senior]] year. At Clemson, he started thirty-three games and recorded a total of 219 tackles, with eight interceptions. During his senior year, he was a first-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] and was a finalist for the [[Jim Thorpe Award]].

==Professional career==
===Early career===
Edwards was selected in the first round of the 1999 NFL Draft by the Green Bay Packers, the first of three consecutive defensive backs the Packers would take in that draft; the others being [[Fred Vinson (American football)|Fred Vinson]] and [[Mike McKenzie (cornerback)|Mike McKenzie]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1999 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1999/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-28 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Edwards would play all sixteen games of his rookie season, starting one of them.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antuan Edwards 1999 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/EdwaAn21/gamelog/1999/ |access-date=2025-06-07 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During the course of the year, he made a total of thirty tackles (twenty-six solo), had four interceptions including one returned for a touchdown, and was named to the ''College & Pro Football Weekly'' All-Rookie team. The following season, he started three games but saw his tackle total go down to twenty-five, while defending nine passes and two interceptions. Edwards only played in three games in 2001 when he suffered a knee injury and was placed on injured reserve. In 2002, he started the season as the team's starting safety, but was replaced early on by rookie [[Marques Anderson]] following a forearm injury. He spent the rest of the season as a backup and totaled forty-four tackles.

===Later career===
He beat out Anderson for the starting job in [[2003 NFL season|2003]] and started a career-high twelve games, and recorded 51 tackles. He would finish the season on [[injured reserve]] following a late-season injury. He left the Packers at the end of the season to join the [[Miami Dolphins]]. He started eight games for the team and had 35 tackles when he was released from the team. He was claimed by the [[St. Louis Rams]], where he ended the season with five starts and 30 more tackles. Edwards then signed with the [[New England Patriots]] but was cut, and signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]]. He started one game and had eleven tackles for the season, but was cut early on. He joined the [[Washington Redskins]], but was released early in camp.
