'''Antwan Fontain Goodley Jr.''' (born September 6, 1991) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor]].

==Early life==
Goodley attended [[Midland High School (Midland, Texas)|Midland High School]] in [[Midland, Texas]]. He played wide receiver, cornerback and returned kicks. He was a three-year starter under head coach Craig Yenzer.  As a senior, he was named first-team All-District 2-5A and first-team All-Permian Basin (by Odessa American) after totaling 613 yards on 38 receptions and four touchdown catches, four rushes for 55 yards and one rushing touchdown, and three touchdowns on kick returns. He finished his career with school-record 1,747 receiving yards. He was ranked by [[ESPN.com]] as the 73rd best receiver in the nation.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/player/news/_/id/94632/antwan-goodley |title=Football Recruiting - Antwan Goodley - Player Profiles - ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date= |access-date=November 2, 2013}}</ref> and 119th by [[Scout.com]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scout.com/a.z?s=143&p=8&c=1&nid=3867221 |title=Antwan Goodley Profile |publisher=Scout.com |date= |accessdate=November 2, 2013}}</ref>

In [[track and field|track]], he won the 200 meters at the 2008 District 3-5A Meet with a time of 21.82 seconds.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://tx.milesplit.com/athletes/244673-antwan-goodley/feed#.VAWDAPmSwrk|title=Antwan Goodley - Feed}}</ref> He was also part of the 4x100 relay team that set the school record with a time of 41.06 seconds. He currently holds the school's fastest [[200 meters|200-meter dash]] time ever, at 21.4 seconds.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mrt.com/sports/top_stories/article_8f2db295-d0e6-5558-9504-8a90b2ed6387.html|title=Bulldogs' Antwan Goodley sets sights on Waco, Baylor|date=February 2, 2010}}</ref>

==College career==
Goodley played college football at [[Baylor University]] from 2010 to 2014. During his collegiate career, he earned All-American honors as a wide receiver and recorded 150 receptions for 2,366 yards and 21 touchdowns.

==Professional career==
===Dallas Cowboys===
Goodley signed with the Dallas Cowboys as an undrafted free agent on May 2, 2015. On September 1, 2015, he was released by the Cowboys.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2015/09/01/cowboys-release-four-make-six-roster-moves-meet-75-man-limit |title=Cowboys Release Four, Make Six Roster Moves To Meet 75-Man Limit |last=Helman |first=David |date=September 1, 2015 |website=DallasCowboys.com |accessdate=September 29, 2015}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
On December 9, 2015 Goodley was signed to the Seahawks practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mynorthwest.com/292/2866701/Seahawks-waive-TE-Chase-Coffman-now-have-two-open-roster-spots |title=Seahawks waive TE Chase Coffman, now have two open roster spots |last=Henderson |first=Brady |date=December 9, 2015 |website=mynorthwest.com}}</ref>

On September 3, 2016, Goodley was released by the Seahawks as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seattle Seahawks Set 53-Man Roster, Trade For Defensive Backs L.J. McCray And Dewey McDonald|url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2016/09/03/seattle-seahawks-set-53-man-roster-trade-defensive-backs-lj-mccray-and-dewey|website=Seahawks.com|date=September 3, 2016|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170806021632/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2016/09/03/seattle-seahawks-set-53-man-roster-trade-defensive-backs-lj-mccray-and-dewey|archivedate=August 6, 2017}}</ref> On September 13, 2016, he was signed to the Seahawks' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign Fullback Will Tukuafu And Cornerback Neiko Thorpe|url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2016/09/13/seahawks-sign-fullback-will-tukuafu-and-cornerback-neiko-thorpe|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170804014208/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2016/09/13/seahawks-sign-fullback-will-tukuafu-and-cornerback-neiko-thorpe|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 4, 2017|last=Boyle|first=John|website=Seahawks.com|date=September 13, 2016}}</ref> He was released on September 27, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign Running Back Zac Brooks, Offensive Lineman Robert Myers To Practice Squad|url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2016/09/27/seahawks-sign-running-back-zac-brooks-offensive-lineman-robert-myers-practice-squad|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|accessdate=September 27, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160929182503/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2016/09/27/seahawks-sign-running-back-zac-brooks-offensive-lineman-robert-myers-practice-squad|archive-date=September 29, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Green Bay Packers===
On December 27, 2016, Goodley was signed to the Packers practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers sign WR Goodley to practice squad|url=http://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-roster-moves/article-1/Packers-sign-WR-Goodley-to-practice-squad/b6a38c73-256f-41b9-bbf6-e730984f493d|website=Packers.com|date=December 27, 2016|access-date=December 27, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161228124546/http://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-roster-moves/article-1/Packers-sign-WR-Goodley-to-practice-squad/b6a38c73-256f-41b9-bbf6-e730984f493d|archive-date=December 28, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He signed a futures contract with the Packers on January 24, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers sign eight free agents|url=http://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-roster-moves/article-1/Packers-sign-eight-free-agents/c28d35fc-65e5-4752-9416-f9f8b7fcf977|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171019192623/http://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-roster-moves/article-1/Packers-sign-eight-free-agents/c28d35fc-65e5-4752-9416-f9f8b7fcf977|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 19, 2017|website=Packers.com|date=January 24, 2017}}</ref> He was waived/injured by the Packers on May 8, 2017 and was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers sign five tryout players from rookie orientation|url=http://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-press-release/article-1/Packers-sign-five-tryout-players-from-rookie-orientation/2ff60d3f-ccbc-4dbf-b795-e45c09dce57e|website=Packers.com|date=May 8, 2017|access-date=May 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170512015515/http://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-press-release/article-1/Packers-sign-five-tryout-players-from-rookie-orientation/2ff60d3f-ccbc-4dbf-b795-e45c09dce57e|archive-date=May 12, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was waived from injured reserve on June 15, 2017.

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On July 28, 2017, Goodley signed with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], only to be waived/injured three days later and placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs Sign WR Antwan Goodley, Cut WR Alonzo Moore|url=http://nfltraderumors.co/chiefs-sign-wr-antwan-goodley-cut-wr-alonzo-moore/|author=Bouda, Nate|date=July 28, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs sign two wide receivers|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/08/01/chiefs-sign-two-wide-receivers/|author=Alper, Josh|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=August 1, 2017}}</ref> He was released on August 22, 2017.

===Baltimore Brigade===
On April 6, 2019, Goodley was assigned to the [[Baltimore Brigade]]. On April 12, 2019, he was placed on recallable reassignment and became a free agent.

===Oklahoma Flying Aces===
On January 1, 2024, Goodley signed with the [[Oklahoma Flying Aces]] of the [[National Arena League]] (NAL).<ref>{{cite web | url= https://m.facebook.com/story.php?story_fbid=pfbid0F9EPPSpWtFj6QHW21gknJqMajHXJvi4ZxXje97wNCpvmGid6J3fsQvVtZnYuJoG9l&id=100039815695580 | title=No better way to hit the ground running on the first day of the year than to announce a former 1st Team All American & All Big 12 player | publisher=Oklahoma Flying Aces | date=January 1, 2024 | accessdate=January 2, 2024}}</ref>

'''Arceto Martinez Clark''' (born September 29, 1989) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Mississippi State]]. He signed with the [[Seattle Seahawks]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2013. With the Seahawks, he won [[Super Bowl XLVIII]] over the [[Denver Broncos]].

==Early life==
Clark was born in [[Tupelo, Mississippi|Tupelo]], [[Mississippi]]. A graduate of [[Lee County School District (Mississippi)|Shannon High School]] in [[Shannon, Mississippi]], Clark was selected to play in the Mississippi-Alabama High School All-Star game at the wide receiver position.<ref name="MISSI">{{cite web | title=Mississippi State Profile  | work=hailstate.com | url=http://www.hailstate.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=16800&ATCLID=1507242 }}</ref> He was ranked among the top 25 high school recruits in the state of Mississippi by ''[[The Clarion-Ledger]]'' following the conclusion of his senior season.<ref name="MISSI" /> He was selected as the Class 4A Division 4 Offensive Most Valuable Player  in high school.<ref name="MISSI" />

==Professional career==

===Seattle Seahawks===
On June 4, 2013, Clark signed with the [[Seattle Seahawks]] as an undrafted free agent.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crabtree |first=Curtis |date=August 13, 2013 |title=Seahawks sign receiver Arceto Clark |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/06/04/seahawks-sign-receiver-arceto-clark/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150721213014/http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/eye-on-football/23400230/final-nfl-cuts-teams-trim-rosters-down-to-53-players |archive-date=July 21, 2015 |access-date=June 4, 2013 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref> On August 31, 2013, he was released by the Seahawks.<ref>{{cite web | title=2013 Final NFL Cuts: Teams trim rosters down to 53 players
| work=cbssports.com | url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/eye-on-football/23400230/final-nfl-cuts-teams-trim-rosters-down-to-53-players |access-date=September 10, 2013}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
On September 10, 2013, Clark signed with the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{cite web |date=September 10, 2013 |title=Browns sign Arceto Clark, Dennis Johnson to practice squad, cut Mount Union product Jasper Collins |url=http://www.ohio.com/blogs/cleveland-browns/cleveland-browns-1.270107/browns-sign-arceto-clark-dennis-johnson-to-practice-squad-cut-mount-union-product-jasper-collins-1.427708 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150602140059/http://www.ohio.com/blogs/cleveland-browns/cleveland-browns-1.270107/browns-sign-arceto-clark-dennis-johnson-to-practice-squad-cut-mount-union-product-jasper-collins-1.427708 |archive-date=June 2, 2015 |access-date=September 10, 2013 |work=Ohio.com}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (second stint)===
On October 2, 2013, Clark re-signed with the [[Seattle Seahawks]] to join the practice squad.<ref name="KFFL">{{cite web|url=http://www.kffl.com/player/28343/nfl/news/arceto-clark |title=Arceto Clark |publisher=kffl.com |access-date=November 30, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029032018/http://www.kffl.com/player/28343/nfl/news/arceto-clark |archive-date=October 29, 2014 }}</ref> He was part of the team that won Super Bowl XLVIII.<ref name="k048">{{cite web | last=Shpigel | first=Ben | title=Forget Forecast: Seahawks Pour It On in the Super Bowl | website=The New York Times | date=2014-02-03 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/02/03/sports/football/start-to-finish-its-all-seahawks.html | access-date=2024-11-05}}</ref> He was released by the Seahawks on August 30, 2014.<ref name="KFFL"/>

'''Antonio Morrison''' (born December 6, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]], and was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the fourth round of the [[2016 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Morrison lived in [[Bellwood, Illinois]], and [[Romeoville, Illinois]], before settling in [[Bolingbrook, Illinois]], where he attended [[Bolingbrook High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adam L. Jahns |date=Jan 27, 2016 |title=Bolingbrook's Antonio Morrison has Bears', NFL's attention |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2016/1/27/18464267/bolingbrook-s-antonio-morrison-has-bears-nfl-s-attention |access-date=March 3, 2021 |website=chicago.suntimes.com}}</ref> He was a three-year [[varsity sports|varsity]] starter for the football team. As a senior [[linebacker]] in 2011, Morrison was named 1st Team All-State after leading Bolingbrook to an [[Illinois High School Association|IHSA]] Class 8A State Championship. After the season, Morrison participated in the Semper Fidelis [[All-American]] Bowl in [[Phoenix, Arizona]]. He was named a [[USA Today All-USA high school football team|''USA Today'' 2nd Team All-American]].

Rated a 4-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Morrison committed to [[Florida Gators football|Florida]] in August 2011 shortly before his senior season. He chose the Gators over numerous offers that included [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]] and [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon]].

==College career==
In July 2013, Morrison was charged with interfering with a police animal after barking at a police dog. The charge was dropped after it was determined that Morrison acted without malice. He was suspended for 2 games for the incident by Florida head coach [[Will Muschamp]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goodbread |first=Chase |date=July 23, 2013 |title=Antonio Morrison charge for barking at police dog dropped |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap1000000220030/article/antonio-morrison-charge-for-barking-at-police-dog-dropped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130727034407/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap1000000220030/article/antonio-morrison-charge-for-barking-at-police-dog-dropped |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 27, 2013 |access-date=April 30, 2016 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

On January 3, 2015, Morrsion played in the [[2015 Birmingham Bowl (January)|2015 Birmingham Bowl]], but left the Gators 28–20 victory over [[East Carolina Pirates football|East Carolina]] in the second quarter after he suffered a knee injury while making a [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackle]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jordan McPherson |date=January 6, 2015 |title=Notebook: Antonio Morrison injures knee in Birmingham Bowl |url=http://www.alligator.org/sports/football/article_bc962044-9563-11e4-b32d-532e137c94e1.html |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=alligator.com}}</ref> While covering a [[screen pass]] to an East Carolina [[running back]], Morrison and a teammate playing [[defensive lineman]] both converged the East Carolina player to make the tackle. Morrison's teammate accidentally collided with his planted left leg. He immediately crumbled to the ground, clutching his left leg and began screaming in pain uncontrollably. The following day, Morrison was diagnosed with torn ligaments and a [[torn ACL]] in his left knee. His injury was described as devastating and Morrison was told he may never normally walk again, let alone return to football. The injury, dramatically changed Morrison's initial plan to forgo his senior season and enter the [[2015 NFL draft]]. He had two surgeries on January 9, 2014 and February 23, 2015. Morrison was given a ten-month timetable to fully recovery, but managed to return in six months and was given the permission to return to football the following month in August.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Edward Aschoff |date=December 3, 2015 |title=How Antonio Morrison came back from a devastating knee injury to lead Florida's defense |url=http://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/14279321/florida-gators-star-linebacker-antonio-morrison-incredible-comeback |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

In four seasons with the Florida Gators, Morrison compiled 315 total tackles, 21 [[tackles-for-loss]], 4.5 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]], 1 [[interception]], and 3 forced [[fumble]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Morrison profile |url=http://floridagators.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2168 |access-date=April 30, 2016 |website=floridagators.com}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===

====2016====
The [[Indianapolis Colts]] selected Morrison in the fourth round (125th overall) of the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Morrison was the 18th linebacker selected in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Josh Wilson |date=April 30, 2016 |title=Colts draft Florida linebacker Antonio Morrison in fourth round of NFL Draft |url=https://www.stampedeblue.com/2016/4/30/11544762/colts-draft-florida-linebacker-antonio-morrison-in-fourth-round-of-nfl-draft |access-date=February 15, 2018 |website=stampedeblue.com}}</ref> On May 6, 2016, the Colts signed Morrison to a four-year, $2.85 million contract that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $519,906.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 6, 2016 |title=Indianapolis Colts sign fourth round draft pick LB-Antonio Morrison |url=http://blogs.colts.com/2016/05/06/indianapolis-colts-sign-fourth-round-draft-pick-lb-antonio-morrison/ |access-date=May 6, 2016 |website=blogs.colts.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Antonio Morrison contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/indianapolis-colts/antonio-morrison-19079/ |access-date=February 15, 2018 |website=spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]], Morrison competed against [[Sio Moore]], [[Nate Irving]], [[Amarlo Herrera]], Junior Sylvestre, and [[Edwin Jackson (American football)|Edwin Jackson]] in an open competition for the vacant starting inside linebacker role after [[Jerrell Freeman]] departed during free agency.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mike Chapelle |date=July 20, 2016 |title=Colts linebacker Nate Irving looking for more in 2nd season |url=http://fox59.com/2016/05/20/colts-linebacker-nate-irving-looking-for-more-in-2nd-season/ |access-date=February 15, 2018 |website=fox59.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Josh Wilson |date=July 26, 2016 |title=Ted Monachino on Colts inside linebacker competition: "We've got three really good players there" |url=https://www.stampedeblue.com/2016/7/26/12286782/ted-monachino-inside-linebacker-competition-three-really-good-players-colts-nate-irving-sio-moore |access-date=February 15, 2018 |website=stampedeblue.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Chuck Pagano]] named Morrison the fourth inside linebacker on the depth chart to begin the regular season, behind [[D'Qwell Jackson]], Moore, and [[Josh McNary]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kevin Bowen |date=September 6, 2016 |title=Colts Release 2016 Regular Season Depth Chart |url=http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Colts-Release-2016-Regular-Season-Depth-Chart/b0d13328-534f-488f-9845-abc94298b12a |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180216205320/http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Colts-Release-2016-Regular-Season-Depth-Chart/b0d13328-534f-488f-9845-abc94298b12a |archive-date=February 16, 2018 |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=Colts.com}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the Colts' season-opener against the [[Detroit Lions]] and made one solo tackle during their 39–35 loss. Morrison made his first career tackle on tight end [[Eric Ebron]] after he caught a 13-yard pass from [[Matthew Stafford]] in the second quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 11, 2016 |title=NFL Game Center: Week-2016: Detroit Lions @ Indianapolis Colts |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2016091111/2016/REG1/lions@colts |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On December 11, 2016, Morrison earned his first career start in place of Jackson after Jackson suffered a [[concussion]] during a Week 13 victory over the [[New York Jets]] and was placed in the concussion protocol.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fox Sports |date=June 30, 2016 |title=Colts Injury Update: D'Qwell Jackson, Denzelle Good Enter League's Concussion Protocol |url=https://www.foxsports.com/nfl/story/colts-injury-update-d-qwell-jackson-denzelle-good-enter-league-s-concussion-protocol-120616 |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=FoxSports.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Josh Wilson |date=December 11, 2016 |title=Colts inactives vs. Texans include several injured starters |url=https://www.stampedeblue.com/platform/amp/2016/12/11/13912258/colts-inactives-vs-texans-include-several-injured-starters |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=stampedeblue.com}}</ref> He finished the Colts' 22–17 loss to the [[Houston Texans]] with nine combined tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 14-2016: Houston Texans @ Indianapolis Colts |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2016121104/2016/REG14/texans@colts |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On December 24, 2016, Morrison collected a season-high 11 combined tackles as the Colts' lost 33–25 at the [[Oakland Raiders]]. Morrison finished his rookie season in 2016 with 52 combined tackles (33 solo) in 16 games and four starts.<ref name="career" /> The Indianapolis Colts finished the 2016 season third in the [[AFC South]] with an 8–8 record and did not qualify for the playoffs. [[Pro Football Focus]] (PFF) ranked Morrison the third most efficient tackler among rookies in 2016 with a tackling efficiency grade of 12.3.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kevin Hickey |date=July 13, 2016 |title=Colts' Antonio Morrison among most efficient tacklers in 2016 |url=https://coltswire.usatoday.com/2017/07/13/indianapolis-colts-antonio-morrison-most-efficient-tacklers/ |access-date=February 16, 2017 |website=coltswire.usatoday.com}}</ref>

====2017====
Defensive coordinator [[Ted Monachino]] stated the Colts would hold an open competition during organized team activities and training camp to name a new starting inside linebackers to replace longtime veteran D'Qwell Jackson, who was released after the 2016 season. The competition included Morrison, [[Jon Bostic]], [[Sean Spence]], [[Luke Rhodes]], Edwin Jackson, and rookie [[Anthony Walker Jr.]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kevin Hickey |date=August 31, 2017 |title=Colts' Antonio Morrison seeing a lot of work with first-team |url=https://coltswire.usatoday.com/2017/08/03/indianapolis-colts-antonio-morrison-work-first-team/ |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=coltswire.usatoday.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Stephen Holder |date=February 17, 2017 |title=Colts release linebacker D'Qwell Jackson |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nfl/colts/2017/02/09/colts-release-linebacker-dqwell-jackson/97701770/?from=new-cookie |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=indystar.com}}</ref> Head coach Chuck Pagano named Morrison and Jon Bostic the starting inside linebackers, along with outside linebackers [[John Simon (linebacker)|John Simon]] and [[Jabaal Sheard]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stephen Holder |date=September 6, 2017 |title=Insider: Breaking down the Colts' depth chart |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nfl/colts/2017/09/07/insider-breaking-down-colts-depth-chart/640668001/?from=new-cookie |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=indystar.com}}</ref>

He started the Colts' season-opener at the [[Los Angeles Rams]] and recorded four combined tackles as the Colts were routed 46–9. The following week, he was inactive due to a [[groin]] injury and missed the Colts' 16–13 loss to the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andrew Ites |date=September 13, 2017 |title=Colts Injury Report: Morrison, Walker Day-to-Day, Rogers Returns |url=https://www.horseshoeheroes.com/2017/09/13/colts-injury-report-two-lbs-day-day-chester-rogers-back/ |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=horseshoeheroes.com}}</ref> On October 22, 2017, he recorded a season-high 14 combined tackles during a 27–0 loss to the Jaguars. In Week 15, Morrison made 12 combined tackles in the Colts' 25–13 loss to the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antonio Morrsion (2017) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antoniomorrison/2555160/gamelogs?season=2017 |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He completed his second season with a total of 109 combined tackles (64 solo) and one pass deflection in 15 games and 15 starts.<ref name="career">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Antonio Morrison (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/antoniomorrison/2555160/careerstats |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Head coach Chuck Pagano was fired after the Colts finished 4–12 and did not qualify for the playoffs. The Colts' linebacker corps was weakest part of their defense. PFF gave Morrison an overall grade of 35.8 and it ranked 83rd among all linebackers in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pro Football Focus: Antonio Morrsion |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/nfl/players/antonio-morrison/10759 |access-date=February 16, 2018 |website=ProFootballFocus.com}}</ref>

===Green Bay Packers===
On August 26, 2018, Morrison was traded to the [[Green Bay Packers]] in exchange for cornerback [[Lenzy Pipkins]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 26, 2018 |title=Packers acquire LB Antonio Morrison in trade with Colts |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-acquire-lb-antonio-morrison-in-trade-with-colts |website=Packers.com}}</ref> He recorded his first career sack on November 4, 2018, on [[New England Patriots]] quarterback [[Tom Brady]].

On March 8, 2019, the Packers waived Morrison.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nash |first=Anthony |date=March 8, 2019 |title=Packers release linebacker Antonio Morrison |url=https://packerswire.usatoday.com/2019/03/08/packers-release-linebacker-antonio-morrison/ |access-date=March 9, 2019 |website=PackersWire}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=March 8, 2019 |title=Packers release LB Antonio Morrison |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-release-lb-antonio-morrison |website=packers.com}}</ref>

'''Leander Antwione Williams''' (born May 26, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for the [[Detroit Lions]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Southern Eagles football|Georgia Southern Eagles]], and was selected by the Lions in the fifth round of the [[2016 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Williams attended [[Lovejoy High School (Georgia)|Lovejoy High School]] where he was a two-tme All-Regional selection. He was named All-county and All-South Crescent in 2009 and 2010. For his career, he recorded 63 [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]] (14 solo), eight [[tackles-for-loss]], three [[Quarterback sack|sacks]], four [[interception]]s, eight [[passes defensed]], two blocked kicks and one [[touchdown]].<ref name="College bio">{{cite web |url=https://gseagles.com/sports/football/roster/antwione-williams/1461 |title=Antwione Williams - Football |website=Georgia Southern University Athletics |access-date=September 19, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
Williams then attended [[Georgia Southern University]] where he [[Major (academic)|majored]] in [[psychology]].<ref name="College bio" />

As a freshman in [[2011 Georgia Southern Eagles football team|2011]], he appeared in 11 games, starting three at [[linebacker]]. He finished the season with 25 tackles and one tackle-for-loss. In [[2012 Georgia Southern Eagles football team|2012]] as a sophomore, he appeared in 14 games, starting six. He recorded 32 tackles (17 solo) and three passes defensed. He then missed the [[2013 Georgia Southern Eagles football team|2013]] with an injury and was given a medical [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]]. In [[2014 Georgia Southern Eagles football team|2014]], he returned as a redshirt junior and started all 12 games. He finished second on the team with 65 tackles (44 solo), eight tackles-for-loss, three sacks, one forced [[fumble]] and four passes defensed. For the season, he was named an All-[[Sun Belt Conference]] honorable mention. He also was named to the [[Dean's list]] in the spring and was a member of the Eagle Honor Roll for the spring as well. As a redshirt senior in [[2015 Georgia Southern Eagles football team|2015]], he started all 13 games. He recorded 107 tackles (48 solo), 10.5 tackles-for-loss, four sacks, four forced fumbles, two quarterback hurries and three passes defensed. After the season, he was named an All-Sun Belt honorable mention selection.<ref name="College bio" />

Williams was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the fifth round (169th overall) of the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On May 6, he signed his four-year rookie contract.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2016/05/05/detroit-lions-2016-draft-signings/83992988/ |title=Detroit Lions sign three more draft picks to 4-year deals |last=Birkett |first=Dave |newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=May 6, 2016 |access-date=September 19, 2016}}</ref> He played 14 games for the Lions in 2016, recording 17 solo tackles, 27 total tackles, and one QB hit on the season. On September 2, 2017, Williams was waived by the Lions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions establish 53-man roster|url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-establish-53-man-roster/afd5f964-b8d1-4f20-8b0b-055acb8905ac|website=DetroitLions.com|date=September 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170903005052/https://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-establish-53-man-roster/afd5f964-b8d1-4f20-8b0b-055acb8905ac|archive-date=September 3, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On September 13, Williams was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Sign Former Lions LB Antwione Williams to Practice Squad|url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Sign-Former-Lions-LB-Antwione-Williams-to-Practice-Squad/8ed42568-9767-4fcd-af92-339c92a9e9b9?sf113784538=1|website=Vikings.com|date=September 13, 2017|access-date=September 13, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170914004014/http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Sign-Former-Lions-LB-Antwione-Williams-to-Practice-Squad/8ed42568-9767-4fcd-af92-339c92a9e9b9?sf113784538=1|archive-date=September 14, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Vikings on January 22, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Sign 6 to Reserve/Future Contracts|url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Sign-6-to-ReserveFuture-Contracts/494b80de-fcf4-4a7c-96a0-fbabf6cd4ade|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180331001755/http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Sign-6-to-ReserveFuture-Contracts/494b80de-fcf4-4a7c-96a0-fbabf6cd4ade|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 31, 2018|website=Vikings.com|date=January 22, 2018}}</ref> On August 31, Williams was waived by the Vikings.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Release 14 Players|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-release-14-players|website=Vikings.com|date=August 31, 2018}}</ref>

On September 3, Williams was signed to the [[Seattle Seahawks]]' practice squad, but was released two days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Set 53-Man Roster|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-set-53-man-roster|website=Seahawks.com|date=September 1, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks re-sign Branden Jackson, release Antwione Williams|url=https://247sports.com/nfl/seattle-seahawks/Article/Branden-Jackson-re-sign-Antwione-Williams-released-121466299/|website=247sports.com|date=September 5, 2018}}</ref>

On December 19, Williams was signed to the [[Carolina Panthers]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |last=Strickland |first=Bryan |date=December 19, 2018 |title=Panthers place Graham Gano on injured reserve |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-place-graham-gano-on-injured-reserve |access-date=March 14, 2026 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Panthers on December 31.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers sign 13 players to future contracts|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-sign-13-players-to-future-contracts|website=Panthers.com|date=December 31, 2018}}</ref> He was waived during final roster cuts on August 30, 2019.<ref>{{cite news |last=Henson |first=Max |title=Panthers announce first wave of 2019 roster cuts |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-announce-first-wave-of-2019-roster-cuts-artis-payne-corn-elder |website=Panthers.com |date=August 30, 2019 |access-date=August 30, 2019}}</ref>

Williams was signed by the [[DC Defenders]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]] during [[mini-camp]] in December 2019. He was waived on February 29, 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=XFL Transactions |url=https://www.xfl.com/xfl-transactions |website=XFL.com |access-date=March 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200316152142/https://www.xfl.com/xfl-transactions |archive-date=March 16, 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In August 2020, Williams began attending [[Atlanta's John Marshall Law School]] and graduated in May 2023 with a [[Juris Doctor]] degree.

On November 7, 2024, Williams was charged with felonies of civil disorder and assaulting, resisting or impeding police, along with several lesser misdemeanor charges, in connection with the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|January 6 riots at the US Capitol]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Mike |last=Wendling |title=Former NFL player charged in Jan 6 Capitol riot |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c3demk493zmo |work=[[BBC News]] |access-date=November 14, 2024 |date=November 14, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://justice.gov/usao-dc/pr/georgia-man-charged-assaulting-law-enforcement-and-other-offenses-during-jan-6-capitol|title=Georgia Man Charged with Assaulting Law Enforcement and Other Offenses During Jan. 6 Capitol Breach|type=Press release|location=[[Washington, D.C.]]|publisher=[[United States Department of Justice]]|date=November 14, 2024|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260521065502/https://justice.gov/usao-dc/pr/georgia-man-charged-assaulting-law-enforcement-and-other-offenses-during-jan-6-capitol|archive-date=May 21, 2026|access-date=June 16, 2026}}</ref> On January 20, 2025, he was among those [[Pardon of January 6 United States Capitol attack defendants|pardoned by President Trump]] for their actions in the January 6 attack.<ref>{{cite news |title=45 Michiganians benefit from Trump's reversal of Jan. 6 punishments, prosecution |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2025/01/20/trump-issues-pardons-for-participants-in-jan-6-riot-at-the-u-s-capitol/77842157007/ |work=[[The Detroit News]] |access-date=February 28, 2025 |date=January 21, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Trump Pardons Dozens of Michiganders From Crimes Related to Jan. 6 Riot |url=https://www.wjr.com/2025/01/21/trump-pardons-dozens-of-michiganders-from-crimes-related-to-jan-6-riot/ |publisher=[[WJR]] |access-date=February 28, 2025 |date=January 21, 2025}}</ref>

'''Antonio Hamilton Sr.''' (born January 24, 1993) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Washington Commanders]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[South Carolina State Bulldogs football|South Carolina State Bulldogs]]. Hamilton signed with the [[Oakland Raiders]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2016 and has also been a member of several other NFL teams.

== College career ==
Hamilton attended [[South Carolina State University]]. While there he played for three seasons in a total of 33 games. He recorded 73 tackles, one [[Quarterback sack|sack]], four [[interception]]s, and nine passes defensed.  In addition, he recorded 33 [[kickoff return]]s for 818 yards and two [[touchdown]]s as well as 23 [[Punt (gridiron football)|punt]] [[Punt return|returns]] for 498 yards and two touchdowns. As a junior, he earned All-[[Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference|Conference]] honors as a [[return specialist]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oakland Raiders: Antonio Hamilton |url=http://www.raiders.com/team/roster/Antonio-Hamilton/375ff718-dc24-4300-8e44-02e81e6a1c9b |access-date=October 5, 2016 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref>

'''ArDarius Stewart''' (born December 8, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]], and was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the third round of the [[2017 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Stewart attended [[Fultondale High School (1965–2021)|Fultondale High School]] in [[Fultondale, Alabama]], a suburb outside of [[Birmingham, Alabama|Birmingham]], where he played on the Wildcats [[High school football|football]] team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Harris |first=Erik |date=April 28, 2017 |title=ArDarius Stewart becomes first Fultondale Wildcat selected in NFL Draft |url=http://www.njeffersonnews.com/sports/ardarius-stewart-becomes-first-fultondale-wildcat-selected-in-nfl-draft/article_f2d07ca8-2c52-11e7-97d8-57ff5c7b9174.html |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170709183545/http://www.njeffersonnews.com/sports/ardarius-stewart-becomes-first-fultondale-wildcat-selected-in-nfl-draft/article_f2d07ca8-2c52-11e7-97d8-57ff5c7b9174.html |archive-date=July 9, 2017 |access-date=April 12, 2018 |website=North Jefferson News |language=en}}</ref> He played [[quarterback]], [[running back]], and [[wide receiver]] in high school.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Suttles  |first=Aaron |date=November 28, 2016 |title=Alabama's ArDarius Stewart showing off his versatility this season |url=http://www.tuscaloosanews.com/news/20161129/alabamas-ardarius-stewart-showing-off-his-versatility-this-season |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=Tuscaloosa News}}</ref> Stewart committed to the [[University of Alabama]] to play [[college football]] under head coach [[Nick Saban]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 28, 2012 |title=Ardarius Stewart commits to Crimson Tide |url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Ardarius-Stewart-commits-to-Crimson-Tide-104873341 |access-date=April 12, 2018 |website=BamaOnLine |language=en-US}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
Stewart was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the third round (79th overall) of the 2017 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Ethan |date=April 28, 2017 |title=Jets Select WR ArDarius Stewart in Round 3 |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-select-wr-ardarius-stewart-in-round-3-18796562 |access-date=April 28, 2017 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> On May 25, 2017, Stewart signed a four-year deal with the Jets worth $3.25 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mehta |first=Manish |date=May 25, 2017 |title=Jets sign third-round pick ArDarius Stewart to standard rookie contract |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/football/jets/jets-sign-third-round-pick-ardarius-stewart-rookie-deal-article-1.3196146 |access-date=May 25, 2017 |website=New York Daily News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jets' ArDarius Stewart: Could earn starting job |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/jets-ardarius-stewart-could-earn-starting-job/ |access-date=August 8, 2017 |work=CBS Sports|date=August 8, 2017 }}</ref> On September 10, Stewart made his NFL debut. He had two receptions for 10 yards in the 21–12 loss to the [[Buffalo Bills]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Jets at Buffalo Bills - September 10th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100buf.htm |access-date=September 24, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> Overall, in his rookie season, Stewart finished with six receptions for 82 receiving yards in 15 games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ArDarius Stewart 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/StewAr00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=April 12, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

'''Antony Auclair''' (born May 28, 1993) is a Canadian former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football|university football]] at [[Laval Rouge et Or|Université Laval]], and was signed by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2017, with whom he won [[Super Bowl LV]] in 2020. He also played in the NFL for the [[Houston Texans]].

==Professional career==
===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
Auclair signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 1, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=May 1, 2017 |title=Bucs' Rookie Free Agents Flesh Out Roster |url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Bucs-Rookie-Free-Agents-Flesh-Out-Roster/0bbae856-9641-489b-bc56-2349782ddfb7 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025204801/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Bucs-Rookie-Free-Agents-Flesh-Out-Roster/0bbae856-9641-489b-bc56-2349782ddfb7 |archive-date=October 25, 2017 |access-date=September 6, 2017 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> He made the Buccaneers' 53-man roster as the only undrafted rookie on the team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=September 2, 2017 |title=Wide Variety of Moves Gets Bucs to 53 |url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-1/Wide-Variety-of-Moves-Gets-Bucs-to-53/229beb34-4568-4236-8cc8-4ad794feb408 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170904004035/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-1/Wide-Variety-of-Moves-Gets-Bucs-to-53/229beb34-4568-4236-8cc8-4ad794feb408 |archive-date=September 4, 2017 |access-date=September 3, 2017 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> He was also drafted by the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] in the 4th round, with the 30th overall pick, of the [[2017 CFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=How |first=Harry |date=May 8, 217 |title=Saskatchewan Roughriders draft Cameron Judge second overall |url=http://leaderpost.com/sports/football/saskatchewan-roughriders-draft-cameron-judge-second-overall |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010151832/http://leaderpost.com/sports/football/saskatchewan-roughriders-draft-cameron-judge-second-overall |archive-date=October 10, 2017 |access-date=October 10, 2017 |publisher=leaderpost.com}}</ref>

On November 5, 2019, Auclair was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |date=November 5, 2019 |title=Buccaneers sign Sam Acho, place Antony Auclair on IR |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/11/05/buccaneers-sign-sam-acho-place-antony-auclair-on-ir/ |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref>

Auclair re-signed with the Buccaneers on a one-year contract on March 18, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=March 19, 2020 |title=Bucs Retain TE Antony Auclair |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-sign-antony-auclair-free-agency-2020 |access-date=March 21, 2020 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on September 18, 2020, with a calf injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=September 18, 2020 |title=TE Antony Auclair Lands on Minor IR |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-place-tight-end-antony-auclair-minor-injured-reserve |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> He was activated on October 31.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=October 31, 2020 |title=Antony Auclair Returns to Active Roster |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/antony-auclair-returns-active-roster-move-2020 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210512143837/https://www.buccaneers.com/news/antony-auclair-returns-active-roster-move-2020 |archive-date=May 12, 2021 |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> Auclair earned a Super Bowl championship when the Buccaneers defeated the [[2020 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]] by a score of 31–9 in [[Super Bowl LV]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LV – Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs. Kansas City Chiefs – February 7th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202102070tam.htm |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
Auclair signed with the [[Houston Texans]] on April 14, 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |date=April 14, 2021 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (4-14-2021) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-4-14-2021 |access-date=April 14, 2021 |work=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> He was released on August 31, 2021, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 31, 2021 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (8-31-2021) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-8-31-2021 |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2021 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (9-1-2021) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-9-1-2021 |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> On September 21, Auclair was signed to the active roster.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 21, 2021 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (9-21-2021) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-9-21-2021 |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> In Week 5 of the 2021 season, he scored his first NFL touchdown against the New England Patriots on an 11–yard reception.<ref name="r303">{{cite web | last=Sidhu | first=Deepi | title=Canadian-born Antony Auclair on his first NFL TD and learning from Gronk | website=Houston Texans | date=2021-10-12 | url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/canadian-born-antony-auclair-on-his-first-nfl-td-and-learning-from-gronk-daily-b | access-date=2025-01-18}}</ref>

On March 30, 2022, Auclair re-signed with the Texans.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 30, 2022 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (3-30-2022) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-3-30-2022 |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> He was released on August 30, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2022 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (8-30-2022) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-8-30-2022 |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On October 31, 2022, Auclair signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=October 31, 2022 |title=Titans Waive DB Ugo Amadi From 53-Man Roster While Also Making a Pair of Practice Squad Moves |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-waive-db-ugo-amadi-from-53-man-roster-while-also-making-a-pair-of-practic |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref> Auclair was waived by the Titans on November 21.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=November 21, 2022 |title=Titans Waive K Josh Lambo, Add Two to Practice Squad |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-waive-k-josh-lambo-add-two-to-practice-squad |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref>

On February 1, 2024, Auclair announced his retirement from professional football.<ref name="d046">{{cite web | title=Former Bucs and Texans tight end Antony Auclair announces retirement | website=AP News | date=2024-02-01 | url=https://apnews.com/article/antony-auclair-retirement-05ead5b6b4dd3baddf094350a42d29cb#:~:text=%E2%80%9CAfter%20a%20year%20away%20from,said%20in%20an%20Instagram%20post. | access-date=2024-12-14}}</ref>

'''Antonio Johnson''' (born October 29, 2001) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M Aggies]].

==Early life==
Johnson attended O’Fallon Township High School in O’Fallon, Illinois before transferring to [[East St. Louis Senior High School]] in [[East St. Louis, Illinois]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kvidahl |first=David |title=No. 4: Johnson eager to join recent ring party at East St. Louis |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/high-school/football/super-30/no-4-johnson-eager-to-join-recent-ring-party-at-east-st-louis/article_d2d69046-c835-11e9-a371-df659db6e3a4.html |access-date=May 11, 2023 |website=STLtoday.com |date=August 26, 2019 |language=en}}</ref> He was selected to play in the 2020 [[All-American Bowl (high school football)|All-American Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Criddle |first=Dean |date=January 2, 2020 |title=East St. Louis safety Antonio Johnson impresses during All-American Bowl workouts |url=https://www.bnd.com/sports/high-school/recruiting/article238901183.html |access-date=July 19, 2023 |website=Belleview News-Democrat}}</ref> A four-star prospect, he committed to play [[college football]] at [[Texas A&M University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Halfacre |first=Paul |date=September 21, 2019 |title=East St. Louis DB Johnson commits to Texas A&M |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/high-school/recruiting/football/east-st-louis-db-johnson-commits-to-texas-a-m/article_835897b4-dcbf-11e9-b51f-4735a0f66e59.html/ |access-date=July 19, 2023 |newspaper=St. Louis Today}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Cam |date=September 23, 2019 |title=Despite Auburn loss, Texas A&M gains in recruiting with 4-star Antonio Johnson |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/despite-auburn-loss-texas-am-gains-in-recruiting-with-4-star-antonio-johnson |access-date=July 20, 2023 |website=USA TODAY High School Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Antonio Johnson, Texas A&M Aggies, Safety |url=https://247sports.com/player/antonio-johnson-46051895/ |access-date=September 27, 2022 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
Johnson played in seven games and made one start as a true freshman at Texas A&M in 2020, recording 14 tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Underwood |first=Hannah |date=March 30, 2021 |title=Texas A&M offseason breakout candidates: Is safety Antonio Johnson poised to make an impression as a sophomore? |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/texas-am-aggies/2021/03/30/texas-am-offseason-breakout-candidates-is-s-antonio-johnson-poised-to-make-an-impression-in-his-sophomore-season/ |access-date=July 19, 2023 |website=Dallas News}}</ref> As a sophomore in 2021, he started all 12 games and had 79 tackles, an [[interception]], and a [[Quarterback sack|sack]] and was named a member of the [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] second team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zwerneman |first=Brent |date=October 12, 2021 |title=How ‘Friday Night Lights’ helped draw Antonio Johnson to Texas A&M |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/How-Friday-Night-Lights-helped-draw-Antonio-16528318.php |access-date=July 20, 2023 |website=Houston Chronicle |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Cole |date=May 9, 2022 |title=Where Does Texas A&M DB Antonio Johnson Rank Among Early 2023 Draft Prospects? |url=https://www.si.com/college/tamu/news/aggies-2023-draft-antonio-johnson-pro-football-focus-jalen-pitre-leon-o-neal |access-date=July 20, 2023 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Travis L. |date=October 15, 2021 |title=Family of Texas A&M's Antonio Johnson to celebrate his success Saturday close to St. Louis home |url=https://theeagle.com/sports/college/aggiesports/football/family-of-texas-a-ms-antonio-johnson-to-celebrate-his-success-saturday-close-to-st/article_407de2f4-2c73-11ec-8d66-475eae697961.html |access-date=July 19, 2023 |website=The Eagle}}</ref>

'''Antonio Williams''' (born July 14, 2004) is an American professional football [[wide receiver]] for the [[Washington Commanders]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Williams played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] and was selected by the Commanders in the third round of the [[2026 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Williams was born on July 14, 2004, and grew up in [[Greenville, South Carolina]].<ref name="TheBeast">{{cite web |last1=Brugler |first1=Dane |title=Antonio Williams - The Beast 2026 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/interactive/the-beast-2026/player/antonio-williams-clemson-wide-receiver/ |website=The Athletic |publisher=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=May 19, 2026}}</ref> He attended [[Dutch Fork High School]] in [[Irmo, South Carolina]].<ref name="TheBeast"/> During his career, he had 137 receptions for 2,458 yards and 23 [[touchdowns]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yahoo.com/lifestyle/antonio-williams-impressing-early-clemson-010246933.html|title=Antonio Williams impressing early on at Clemson fall camp|date=August 10, 2022|website=Yahoo Life}}</ref> Williams was selected to play in the 2022 [[Under Armour All-America Game]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lexingtonchronicle.com/stories/dutch-forks-antonio-williams-picked-for-under-armour-all-american-game-among-north-south-all-star,598|title=Dutch Fork's Antonio Williams picked for Under Armour All-American Game, among North-South All-Star selections|date=October 18, 2021|website=Lexington County Chronicle}}</ref> He committed to [[Clemson University]] to play college football.<ref>{{cite web | last=Bezjak | first=Lou | title=Clemson wins in-state battle for Dutch Fork four-star receiver Antonio Williams | website=The State | date=2021-12-09 | url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/high-school/prep-football/article256463361.html | access-date=2026-04-28}}</ref><ref>[https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/article264325501.html Local WR Antonio Williams turning heads at Clemson football]</ref>

==College career==
Williams earned immediate playing time his true freshman year at Clemson in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/clemson/clemson-freshman-antonio-williams-quickly-earns-d-j-uiagaleleis-trust/article_a773e104-3495-11ed-aeaa-9bbeb0888dd0.html|title=Clemson freshman Antonio Williams quickly earns D.J. Uiagalelei's trust|first=Jon|last=Blau|date=September 16, 2022|website=Post and Courier}}</ref><ref>[https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article265677871.html Why freshman receiver could be really special for Clemson]</ref> In his first career game he had four receptions for 37 yards.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dothaneagle.com/ap/sports/freshman-receiver-antonio-williams-making-plays-early-and-often-for-clemson-football/article_db5385fa-db35-51c3-b8d9-b41f8f7597ef.html|title=Freshman receiver Antonio Williams making plays early and often for Clemson football}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] for the [[South Florida Bulls football|South Florida Bulls]] and [[Arkansas Razorbacks football|Arkansas Razorbacks]] and was signed as an [[Free agent#Undrafted free agent|undrafted free agent]] by the Buccaneers in 2024. ==Early life== Grier was born on January 18, 2000, in [[Atlanta, Georgia]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GrieAn00.htm|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|title=Antonio Grier Stats}} He attended [[Benjamin Elijah Mays High School]] in Atlanta, playing three seasons of football team while recording 214 [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]], 19.0 [[tackles-for-loss]] (TFLs), six [[Quarterback sack|sacks]], eight forced [[fumble]]s and three [[interception]]s.{{Cite web|url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/roster/antonio-grier/|publisher=[[Arkansas Razorbacks]]|title=Antonio Grier}} He was honorable mention All-Class 6A as a [[Junior (education year)|junior]] and was named the regional defensive player of the year as a [[Senior (education)|senior]]. He signed to play [[college football]] for the [[South Florida Bulls football|South Florida Bulls]] in 2018.{{Cite news|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2023/jan/07/grier-makes-final-decision-to-be-a-hog/|newspaper=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|title=Grier makes final decision to be a Razorback|author=Davenport, Richard|date=January 7, 2023}} ==College career== As a [[freshman]] at South Florida in 2018, Grier appeared in 12 games, posting eight tackles and a fumble recovery.{{Cite web|url=https://gousfbulls.com/sports/football/roster/antonio-grier/13411|publisher=[[South Florida Bulls]]|title=Antonio Grier}} In 2019, he appeared in all 12 games, six as a starter, and made 58 tackles, 8.5 TFLs and 4.0 sacks. The following year, he earned second-team All-[[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) honors after posting 59 tackles, 5.5 TFLs and 3.0 sacks in eight games.{{Cite news|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2022/dec/24/razorbacks-sign-south-florida-lb/|newspaper=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|title=Razorbacks sign South Florida LB|date=December 24, 2022|author=Davenport, Richard}} In 2021, he started 12 games and posted a team-leading 92 tackles with eight TFLs, three sacks and two interceptions, repeating as a second-team All-AAC selection.{{Cite news|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2022/12/12/usf-lb-antonio-grier-announces-decision-to-transfer-to-ucf/|newspaper=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|date=December 12, 2022|title=USF LB
